articleTitle: Power Efficiency Comparison of Electrical Protection Concepts for AC and DC Grid Operation in an Industrial Robot Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In the context of energy savings, industrial direct current (DC) grids are currently a hot topic of discussion. Their strengths include resource savings and the simplified grid integration of DC-based generators such as photovoltaics and storage systems. The selection of electrical components in a functioning protection concept is seen as a challenge. Initial comparative measurements of system efficiency have been carried out on a few initial test systems or simulations. Due to the complexity of the design and the effort involved in measuring, the influences of the protective devices and concepts are often left out of these analyses. The aim of this publication, however, is to supplement an existing efficiency comparison between DC and alternating current (AC) operation of a robot with the influences of the switching and protection concepts. For this purpose, the individual operating equipment for the control-compliant grid integration of an AC grid and of an earthed (DC-TN) and an unearthed (DC-IT) grid were measured in terms of losses. The DC IT grid is less efficient than the DC TN grid, but offers greater protection against electric shock and greater reliability. Load-dependent and load-independent losses exist in all grid types, which generate an exponential loss characteristic with an exponential curve and an offset. In relation to an industrial handling process in electrical engineering, the load-independent losses have a significantly greater effect than the load-dependent losses. With larger currents, the load-dependent component becomes more important. In total, between 0.96 % and 4.8 % of the total power requirement in the application example is accounted for by the switching and protective devices. Despite lower losses due to protective devices in AC operation, more than 10 % less energy is required in the DC grid.

articleTitle: Operating Time Modification by Elliptic Integration in Feedforward Control of One-Time Swing-Up Pendulum Using Finite-Time Settling Functions with Half-Odd-Integer Trigonometric Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this study, feedforward control of the one-time swing of a 1DOF pendulum is performed using a finite-time settling function expressed by half-odd-integer trigonometric functions. The operating time is set to half the natural period of the oscillator, and the periods are half-odd-integer fractions of this operating time. To apply the finite-time settling functions to enable more accurate control of the pendulum, two modifications are proposed to compensate for the nonlinearity of the pendulum. The first method determines the operation time by considering complete elliptic integral of the first kind, which represents the period of half of the target swing-up angle. The second method uses a parameter that modifies the amplitude of the finite-time settling function, derived from the difference in potential energy between the 1DOF pendulum and the linear oscillator. Simulations are performed to evaluate the improvement in the operation of one-time swinging the pendulum up by these modification methods.

Author Keywords: Complete elliptic integral of the first kind

articleTitle: Trace-Driven Verification Framework for Interoperable Digital Twins in Distributed Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Digital twins offer significant potential for advancing smart manufacturing and production. However, their application within distributed control systems, as well as efforts to enhance their interoperability and data verification, has been minimally explored in the existing literature. This results in a lack of comprehensive guidelines for automation engineers. Therefore, there is a critical need to develop graphical, interoperable digital twins based on available standards and a verification framework to improve data exchange for IEC 61499-based systems. This paper proposes a design approach for interoperable digital twins using the Asset Administration Shell (AAS) within IEC 61499-based distributed control systems, coupled with a data verification method based on execution traces. By integrating AAS with IEC 61499, this approach combines real-time monitoring and control of distributed systems using sensor and actuator data with a flexible, standardized method for representing and validating information, as well as managing these systems, thereby enhancing interoperability.

articleTitle: Smart Ironing Appliance using Real-Time Fabric Classification and Automatic Temperature Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Ironing is a common household task that requires careful temperature control to prevent damage to different fabric types. Traditional irons rely on manual temperature adjustment, leading to errors and potential fabric damage. This paper implements an innovative solution to automating iron temperature control using a machine learning-based fabric type classifier. The classifier response is used to adjust the temperature of the iron automatically. By integrating computer vision technology and machine learning techniques with the hardware control system, the proposed solution aims to enhance the ironing experience, reduce fabric damage, and improve energy efficiency with a simple, easy-to-use, cost-effective end product.

articleTitle: A Reactive Power Circular-Chain Control Strategy for Single-Phase Parallel Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In parallel inverter systems, traditional droop control often results in low power-sharing accuracy and significant circulating currents due to mismatched inverter output impedance. To improve power-sharing accuracy and minimize circulating currents, this paper proposes a control strategy for parallel inverters based on reactive power circular-chain adaptive virtual impedance. This strategy combines droop control with Circular Chain Control (3C) to create a circular-chain structure from the reactive power output of each parallel module. By constructing an adaptive virtual impedance that adjusts in real time according to reactive power requirements, this approach compensates for output impedance mismatches, achieving precise reactive power sharing. The effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed control strategy are validated through MATLAB simulations.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Current Regulation Strategies in an Open-End Winding Traction Motor in Terms of Active Thermal Control of Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The problem of thermo cycling is relevant for traction drives especially at low and zero speeds, when the rotating current vector heats up and cools down the power modules twice per electrical revolution. Active thermal control can be used to solve this problem. This paper proposes to use open-end winding machine together with special current regulation technique, which was called nearly constant losses current regulation. The comparative analysis is given for conventional sinusoidal, space vector and nearly constant losses current regulation techniques. The proposed nearly constant losses current regulation allows to decrease temperature deviation of the MOSFET by 88% compared to conventional current regulation methods, which helps to increase reliability and time to failure of the traction inverter.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power Quality in Distribution Systems through Bi-directional Solid-State Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Power quality issues, including voltage sags, swells, harmonic distortion, oscillatory voltage transients, etc. can degrade equipment performance, leading to inefficiencies and costly disruptions. Studying these issues and introducing solutions are essential for maintaining the reliability and efficiency of modern distribution systems. This paper examines and contrasts the benefits of a bidirectional three-stage solid-state transformer (SST) in mitigating power quality issues to traditional transformers. SST introduces reactive power support to improve the system quality by controlling active and reactive power. This paper investigates key power quality issues-voltage sag, swell, harmonic distortion, and oscillatory transients-arising from capacitor bank energizing, focusing on the novel application of solid-state transformers (SSTs) in mitigating these effects. Additionally, it examines SST-based fault isolation across various fault types (three-phase, double line-to-ground, and line-to-ground). Several simulations have been performed using the MATLAB/Simulink platform to highlight the benefits of the Solid-State Transformer (SST) over conventional transformers and cascade multiple-active-bridge SST (CMABSST) types. The proposed SST employs active and reactive power control to alleviate these effects, allowing the SST controller to manage reactive power effectively and provide the required support that makes the system stable and reliable.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Sliding Mode Control for Unmanned Marine Vehicles Under Input Saturation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper investigates the fault-tolerant control (FTC) issue under input saturation and thruster failures in unmanned marine vehicles (UMVs). Firstly, adaptive laws are proposed to estimate the lumped uncertainties of the model. Secondly, an auxiliary system is designed to address the issue of thruster input saturation. Then, an anti-saturation fault-tolerant controller is designed to achieve dynamic positioning (DP) control for UMVs. Different from existing results, the proposed control strategy guarantees stability within a finite time framework. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through simulations on a floating production vessel.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control of Induction Motors: A Comparative Study of Adaptive and Extended Kalman Filter-Based Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Induction motors are widely used in both industrial and domestic applications. These motors are typically driven by power converters to control torque or speed. The controllers require knowledge of the motor's angular speed, which is measured using mechanical sensors. Mechanical sensors are often expensive and fragile. To address this, sensorless control algorithms have been developed, reducing system costs and enhancing system longevity. Despite their advantages, sensorless induction motor control algorithms suffer from being computationally expensive, fragile toward parametric variation, and from delivering very poor performances at low speed. This paper presents and compares three sensorless control algorithms. The first is based on adaptive control theory and Lyapunov functions, while the second and third are different implementations of an Extended Kalman Filter. The three techniques are experimentally tested, and their performance and computational requirements are compared. Finally, conclusions are drawn.

articleTitle: Advanced Control Strategy to Compensate Power Sharing Error and DC Circulating Current in Parallel Single-Phase Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes an advanced control strategy to eliminate both current sharing error and DC circulating current caused by line impedance mismatched and measurement errors in islanded AC microgrid system. The proposed adaptive virtual impedance scheme is developed with the aid of a low bandwidth communication and a simple PI compensator to adaptively adjust the virtual impedance value so that active and reactive power will be shared equally among inverters. Meanwhile, the DC offset in output voltage measurement is detected by using the voltage ripple information of DC link voltage of inverter. The proposed control strategy can be implemented directly without any pre-knowledge of the feeder impedances. The proposed compensation scheme is simple and easy to implement, and it also does not require extra hardware circuit or sensors. The effectiveness of the proposed solution is verified by simulation and experimental results of 6 kVA microgrid system.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Lyapunov Control Method for Bridgeless Boost PFC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: A bridgeless boost power factor corrector (PFC) circuit is widely used in industry to improve the power quality of the system. Conventionally, the boost PFC topology is preferred to perform the power factor improvement task however, the size of the diode bridge increases the volume of the system. The bridgeless boost PFC topology has advantages over the traditional boost-type PFC circuit in terms of the size of the power stage, design complexity, and power loss. In this paper, the performance of the Lyapunov control strategy is investigated for the bridgeless boost PFC system. The design steps of the Lyapunov-based controller are comprehensively given, and the mathematical model is validated using a simulation tool. According to simulation results, the Lyapunov control method offers a good power factor correction performance, and a robust closed-loop behavior is achieved.

articleTitle: Design of A Synchronous Reluctance Motor for Forklift Truck Application Driven from A Low Voltage Battery Pack
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Synchronous Reluctance Motors (SynRMs) emerge as a viable alternative to traditional induction motors for traction application, offering several advantages including robust construction, high-speed capabilities, wide Constant Power Speed Range (CPSR), cost-effectiveness, and enhanced efficiency. This paper outlines the design methodology of a SynRM intended to replace an induction motor of frame size 132M, with an approximately continuous power rating of 8.5 kW, specifically used for forklift truck applications. The validation of the design is achieved through performance analysis using Finite Element Method (FEM)-based simulation software. This study examines the impact of magnetic saturation and cross-coupling effects along the d-axis and q-axis flux paths. Additionally, rotor optimization is performed to enhance torque capability and minimize torque ripple. A comprehensive comparison is presented between the newly designed SynRM and the existing baseline Squirrel Cage Induction Motor (SCIM) utilized in forklift operations. Power factor and efficiency maps for the designed SynRM are generated using Ansys Maxwell simulation software, demonstrating its superior performance characteristics. The findings indicate that the proposed SynRM design not only meets the operational requirements but also offers significant advantages over conventional induction motors.

articleTitle: A Deep Network Based Fault Diagnosis Method for Stabilization Loop of Inertial Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The inertial platform serves as the fundamental component of system navigation, directly affects system performance and safety. Therefore, it is imperative to investigate accurate, fast and reliable fault diagnosis methods. In this paper, a hybrid deep neural network based fault diagnosis method for the inertial platform stable loop is proposed, which consists of the recurrent neural network (RNN), the gated recurrent unit (GRU), and the cross-attention mechanism. RNN is responsible for extracting local high-level features of time series, GRU is used to compensate for global high-level features, and cross-attention can effectively fuse the two features. Ultimately, the efficacy of this method is validated through application to the stabilization loop of the inertial platform. Ultimately, the efficacy of this method is validated through application to the stabilization loop of the inertial platform.

articleTitle: A Path Planning Method for Automated Parking Systems Based on Circular Arcs and Lines with Smoothly Curves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Recently, it is increasing that there are narrow parking spaces which cannot be parked by the present automated parking systems due to gaining the number of automobiles. By combing the existing planning method based on circular arcs and lines with clothoid curves and sigmoid functions, this paper proposes a new path planning method for automated parking systems. In this paper, we show our new path planning method, and the effectiveness of the proposed method is presented by simple numerical simulations.

Author Keywords: Path planning method based on arcs and lines

articleTitle: Enhancing the Cybersecurity of Battery Digital Twins to Ensure the Resilient Supply for Next-Generation Telecommunication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Ensuring the resilience of energy supply is critical for the next generation of telecommunication networks, such as 5G and 6G, which demand high reliability and seamless functionality. This paper addresses the cyber-security challenges of digital twins (DT) used for battery management in telecommunications energy systems. Batteries are pivotal in maintaining the power continuity of telecommunication infrastructure, and DTs enhance their monitoring and fault diagnostics, thereby improving overall system resilience. However, without adequate cybersecurity, DTs themselves can become targets of cyber attacks, risking the system's integrity. This study proposes incorporating additional estimators both at the sensor level and within the DT itself to safeguard against cyber intrusions, specifically targeting false data injection (FDI) attacks. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through simulations of two types of FDI attacks, proving the applicability of the proposed cyber-secured DT framework.

articleTitle: Design the Wind Pendulum Based on Fuzzy PID Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper described the design of a wind pendulum system, comprising four main components: the operative unit, the data acquisition module, the human-computer interaction interface, and the algorithmic core. By leveraging the principles of the simple pendulum and Lissajous curves, the design enabled the wind pendulum to achieve precise linear and circular motions. The control strategy relied on a fuzzy PID control algorithm, which facilitated closed-loop control and enhanced system stability and performance. The schematic design and PCB layout for the control system were created using Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools. Furthermore, MATLAB simulations and experimental validation were conducted to assess the performance of the fuzzy PID algorithm in comparison to traditional PID control. The experimental results revealed that fuzzy PID control not only reduced overshoot, shortened settling time, and improved accuracy, but also greatly improved the wind pendulum's ability to execute fixed linear and circular motions with speed and precision. This approach demonstrated the benefits of fuzzy PID in optimizing dynamic system performance, particularly in applications demanding high precision and rapid response.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Temporal-Magnitude Based Sampling for Event-Based Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In the current industrial environment, which is shifting towards an event-based control prone paradigm, sampling strategies in use must be revisited. Both temporal and magnitude dependent sampling strategies have been demonstrated to be suitable for control systems, reporting benefits in different categories. However, these sampling strategies also present some drawbacks, discussed in this contribution. Aiming to address some of these drawbacks, a new sampling strategy is proposed gathering characteristics of both predecessors.

articleTitle: GMM-Based Distributed Extended Set-Membership Filtering for Target Tracking Under Cyberattacks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: For target tracking in wireless sensor networks under cyberattacks, this paper constructs a Gaussian-mixture-model-based (GMM-based) distributed robust extended set-membership filtering algorithm, aiming to improve the consistency and accuracy of mobile target tracking under malicious cyberattacks. The algorithm is comprised of three sequential steps: correction/measurement update, GMM-based two-cluster clustering fusion and prediction/time update. Firstly, each node utilizes local measurements to update its local prior estimates of the target state and obtain the local posterior estimates of the target state. Secondly, each node conducts GMM-based two-cluster clustering in term of the dissimilarity between all local posterior estimates received from its inneighbors and its prior local estimates. The nodes with smaller dissimilarities are considered to be trusted while those with larger dissimilarities are regarded as non-trusted nodes. The estimates from the non-trusted nodes are excluded, and the trusted ones are included in the fusion step. Finally, each node utilizes the local fused estimates to predict the target state estimates (prior estimates). Experiment results demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method against five common cyberattacks, namely denial of service (DoS), random, false data injection (FDI), replay and hybrid attacks.

articleTitle: Influence of Converter Control on Directional and Fault Identification Algorithms of Protective Relays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The response of power electronics interfaced devices during faults may hinder the accurate operation of protective relays due to the low current injection along with the suppression of negative sequence current. In this regard, some TSOs have defined new grid codes that require the injection of negative sequence current during unbalanced faults. This paper delves into the impact of the negative sequence current injection by power electronics converters on directional relays and fault identification algorithms. Additionally, the influence of the fault resistance and the converter's response time are analyzed by detailed EMT-PSCAD simulations. Results show that it is paramount to inject negative sequence current to properly identify the faults, although it takes longer when compared to a power system based on synchronous generators.

articleTitle: Supervisory Control for Smart Manufacturing Using FIWARE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The problem of providing smart manufacturing units, via supervisor control implemented in FIWARE, is studied. In order to investigate the problem at hand, an indicative manufacturing unit is considered, and the desired safe performance of the unit is achieved via a supervisory control architecture, being implemented in cloud computing environment. The model of the manufacturing unit is developed on the basis of the models of its sensors and actuators, in Discrete Event System (DES) form. The safe behavior of the unit is expressed in the form of nine rules. The rules are translated into nine regular languages that are realized as a set of proper supervisors. The supervisors are analytically determined and conducted in the open platform FIWARE, using all necessary smart data models and platform tools.

articleTitle: Enhancing Reliability in Distributed Generation Systems with Automatic Circuit Reclosers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Automatic Circuit Reclosers (ACRs) are essential self-controlled devices designed to enhance the reliability and efficiency of distribution networks, particularly in systems with distributed generation (DG). This paper explores the functionality, advantages, and optimal integration of ACRs within complex distribution networks. ACRs facilitate precise fault isolation and reduce outage durations by utilizing adaptable time-current curves (TCC) that allow for effective coordination with other protective devices. The study highlights the advanced features of modern ACR systems, such as intelligent electronic devices and adaptive fault detection methods based on Inverse Definite Time Multiplier (IDTM) characteristics, which enable them to manage the fluctuating power flows characteristic of DG environments. Furthermore, we discuss advanced protection strategies specifically designed for fluctuating currents in DG systems, which enhance the ability to differentiate between normal operational conditions and fault scenarios.

articleTitle: Error Dependent Sampling to Reduce Transient Events in Event Based Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: One of the objectives of event-based control is the reduction of generated events to perform an appropriate process control. Among the event generation techniques used to this end, those quantifying the error signal can be found more frequently for its simplicity of implementation. However, they entail a drawback in the form of trade-off between event generation and performance. Aiming to reduce the number of events, specifically in the transient response, without degrading the performance, an error dependent sampling scheme is studied in this work.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Stochastic MPC for Indoor Thermal Environment in Office Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, a novel event-triggered stochastic model predictive control (ET-SMPC) algorithm is proposed to optimize office buildings energy control. Firstly, a thermal resistance-capacitance (RC) network model of indoor temperature and relative humidity is built to accurately describe the indoor thermal environment of office buildings. Additionally, the ET-SMPC algorithm and its convergence analysis are demonstrated to achieve energy consumption reduction while maintaining personnel comfort. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can not only save energy consumption by 38.0%, but also reduce the consumption of communication resources by 29.6%.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Non-Singular Terminal Sliding Mode Trajectory Tracking Control for Underactuated USV
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This article addresses the trajectory tracking control problem of an underactuated unmanned surface vessel (USV) in the presence of external disturbances, model uncertainties, and unmeasurable velocities. First, the mathematical model of the underactuated USV is reformulated using the hand-position approach. Then, a fixed-time extended state observer(FTESO) is designed to estimate both the unknown velocities and disturbances. Following this, a non-segmented fixed-time non-singular terminal sliding mode controller (NFTNTSMC) is developed, guaranteeing that the tracking error converges to zero within a fixed time. The stability and fixed-time convergence of the system are rigorously proven via the Lyapunov method. Ultimately, numerical simulations are conducted to assess the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed control strategy.

Author Keywords: non-segmented fixed-time non-singular terminal sliding mode

articleTitle: Synthesis of Robust PID Controllers with Disturbance Attenuation Performance for Polytopic Uncertain Multi-Input Multi-Output Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a new parameter adjustment law for robust PID control systems with disturbance attenuation performance for polytopic uncertain multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. In the proposed design approach, the problem of designing the parameter adjustment law for robust PID control systems is reduced to a design problem of static output feedback controllers for uncertain MIMO systems. In this paper, we show that the sufficient conditions for the existence of the proposed parameter adjustment law for the robust PID control system can be reduced to the solvability of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Finally, a simple numerical example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed robust PID control system.

articleTitle: Efficient RISCV Peripheral Access Through Library Level Instruction Selection in Rust
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The open RISC-V instruction set architecture (ISA) defines a new era of domain-specific computer architectures by allowing the implementation of custom, application-specific instructions. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to exposing such instructions to the end user in the Rust programming language. The proposed approach discriminates between statically known and unknown values, and automatically emits the appropriate (e.g, immediate- or register to register-type) instruction without changes to the Rust toolchain. We validate the approach by implementing a Peripheral Access Crate (PAC) for the RISC-V Real-Time Hippomenes architecture. Hippomenes introduces CSR (Control and Status Register)-mapped peripherals allowing efficient peripheral access with reduced software overhead (single instruction read-write/set/clear, including 12-bit peripheral address and optional 5-bit immediate field). Our experiments confirm that all software abstraction layers introduced are completely eliminated at compile time. Moreover, for all cases where the LLVM compiler backend can deduce values to be statically known, immediate instruction variants are selected (thus improving performance and reducing register pressure in comparison to register instructions).

articleTitle: Road Sense Construction Approach Based on Friction Compensation for Steer-by-Wire System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The steer-by-wire (SbW) system, which replaces traditional mechanical linkages, represents a significant advancement in steering system development. However, this decoupled design results in the loss of road sense transmission through the hand wheel and diminishes the performance of active return. To address these challenges and provide a convincing steering feel, this paper introduces a road sense construction approach based on explicit model predictive control (EMPC) with friction compensation. Initially, the characteristics of the hand wheel module are analyzed to establish the foundation for controller design and propose a friction model. Subsequently, the target steering feedback torque (SFT) for road sense construction is designed. To ensure precision and real-time performance, a controller based on EMPC with friction feedforward compensation is presented. Experimental validation confirms the authenticity of the design, the tracking accuracy of the controller, and the effectiveness of the disturbance models.

articleTitle: A PSO-Based Backstepping Pseudo-Sliding Mode Speed Controller Design for PMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper addresses a nonlinear controller design for speed control of permanent magnet synchronous motor drives. The nonlinear controller is structured as a backstepping-based pseudo-sliding mode controller. Moreover, the particle swarm optimization method, a nature-based optimization method, is employed to solve the problem of optimum controller gains in the nonlinear control process. In the system of permanent magnet synchronous motor drives, parametric uncertainties are considered to show the effectiveness of both the nonlinear controller structure and optimizing of the controller design gains. Simulation results are carried out to test the designed nonlinear controller method, which has the optimum controller gains, aiming to track the time-varying speed reference in permanent magnet synchronous motor drives.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Meets Digital Twin: The AI Asset Administration Shell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Digital Twin is a trend term that is frequently used in various research areas. It is a digital representation of an object, called asset. In current research, the restriction to a physical object is lifted and virtual objects are considered. The Asset Administration Shell is an approach to create standardized Digital Twins in the context of Industry 4.0. It allows the combination of both physical and digital assets. Another enabler for high-end solutions is Artificial Intelligence. It offers numerous new ideas and solutions, but adds complexity to existing systems. This paper outlines the life cycle of Artificial Intelligence and how a Digital Twin created by the Asset Administration Shell can be used to reduce complexity. Here, the life cycle is split into a total of six phases that are covered by three different submodels, which are proposed within this work. Furthermore, the meta information of these submodels is presented in detail and their interactions are discussed.

articleTitle: Towards the Creation of Legible Octilinear Power Grid Diagrams Using Integer Linear Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper adapts an integer optimization method for the creation of legible power grids diagrams. Specifically, techniques developed for the automatic production of octilinear metro map diagrams of urban transport networks are applied to power grids. Layout legibility constraints are imposed to optimize diagram clarity and operational usability while properly representing the intricate topologies inherent in power grids. The technique is applied to a number of power grids from various European nations. These early findings demonstrate the potential for algorithms to automatically generate grid diagrams that are neat, attractive and an apt base layer for the overlay of real-time network data.

articleTitle: Bayesian Game-Based Comfort Trading Strategies for Temperature Regulation in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a Heating, Ventilating, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) comfort-level trading model designed to incentivize HVAC systems to provide more Frequency Regulation Service (FRS) for the smart grid. The model first categorizes HVAC systems into two layers: a leader layer with low comfort adjustment levels and a follower layer with high comfort adjustment levels. A Stackelberg game is then established between the leader and follower layers to optimize customer utility. Simultaneously, a Bayesian game model is developed for the HVAC systems in the follower layer, which aims to maximize the utility of customers while enabling the leader layer to provide regulatory services. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed comfort trading model effectively keeps HVAC temperature setpoints within acceptable comfort ranges and enhances customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Control of Strict-Feedback Systems with Deferred State Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this article, an event-triggered adaptive tracking control method is proposed for a class of strict-feedback nonlinear systems with model uncertainty and deferred state constraints (DSCs). Using a new transformation function and combining it with a new unified universal barrier function (UUBF), DSCs can be effectively handled. In addition, we propose a new time-varying relative threshold strategy (TRTS) that significantly reduces the pressure of signal transmission by balancing between state constraints and execution intervals. Simulation verification also confirms the benefits of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Hybrid Control with Variable Frequency for Minimum Losses in Multiphase DC-DC Boost Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Controlling multiphase DC-DC converters is critical for performance, energy efficiency, and reliability; but existing methods often face computational challenges and poor adapt-ability. This paper presents a cost-effective solution for average voltage and current control of multiphase interleaved DC-DC converters using classical control principles. The approach combines adaptive feedforward-feedback control with dynamic filters to maintain performance across varying conditions. It dynamically adjusts the frequency to reduce power losses, making it ideal for energy-efficient applications. Experimental validation on a three-phase boost converter with a low-cost microcontroller demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Electronically Controllable Multiphase Sinusoidal Oscillator Using VDGA-Based All Pass Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This article proposes a multiphase sinusoidal oscillator (MSO) based on a first-order grounded capacitor all-pass filters using voltage differencing gain amplifier (VDGA) as active building block. The proposed MSO offers both even and odd phases. This configuration is attractive to an integrated circuit architecture. Not only the oscillation condition is not required but also the output oscillation frequency can be electronically adjusted by input bias currents of the VDGAs, which can be easily modified to both microcontroller and automatic controlled based circuits/systems. The proposed MSO generates a sinusoidal signal for a wide range of frequencies and offers a precise sinusoidal output signal with an acceptable total harmonic distortion (THD). PSpice simulation results confirm different performances of the proposed MSO, they are accordant well to the referred expectations. The total power consumption of the proposed MSO is about 4.25mW for 3-phase and 5.41mW for 4-phase at ±1.2V power supply.

articleTitle: Comparative FFT Analysis of Ten-Step and SPWM Driven Five-Phase Voltage Source Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The growing adoption of multiphase machines in high-power, variable-speed applications demands a detailed understanding of their operational dynamics. This study compares two Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) techniques—Ten-Step Inverter and Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation (SPWM)—in Five-Phase Voltage Source Inverters (VSIs). Simulations conducted using MATLAB/SIMULINK evaluate the spectral quality of output and pole voltages through Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis. FFT analysis identifies harmonic distortions, providing insights into the strengths and limitations of each modulation technique. The results demonstrate how these techniques influence inverter performance and inform optimal selection for specific applications. The Ten-Step Inverter offers distinct benefits in certain scenarios, while SPWM excels in achieving improved spectral quality in others. This research highlights the importance of FFT analysis in choosing modulation strategies for multiphase systems. The findings contribute to advancing the efficiency and reliability of high-power VSIs in industrial settings.

articleTitle: First Evaluation of a Mechanism to Open Doors with the APR-01 Assistant Personal Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes and evaluates a mechanism to open doors with the APR-01 assistant personal robot to enhance its versatility in indoor environments. The specific manipulator is designed as a dedicated mechanical hand to reach, hold and turn the lever of a conventional door handle. The mechanism is first evaluated under manual control to validate its operability, and then a procedure for automatic door handle detection is proposed to enable autonomous door opening. In manual control mode, a user remotely operates the mobile robot and activates the mechanical hand guided by the images provided by a camera located in the robot head. Since the results on manual control were successful, the feasibility of automatic door handle detection is then assessed. In autonomous mode, the mobile robot analyzes the close-range images captured by a camera embedded in the manipulator. This process is performed using a k-means clustering procedure, which automatically classifies relevant elements to detect and locate possible door handles in the image. Results from door handle detection were also successful, suggesting that this information could be used by the robot to self-adjust its position and control the mechanical arm to open doors autonomously.

articleTitle: Domain Adaptation Method for Gear RUL Prediction Integrating Convolutional Attention and Adversarial Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In recent years, deep learning-based methods for predicting gear remaining useful life (RUL) have garnered widespread attention. However, these approaches continue to encounter various obstacles, such as fluctuating operational environments, interference from noise, and a lack of adequate lifespan data samples. To address these issues, this paper proposes an adaptive gear RUL prediction model that combines convolutional block attention mechanisms (CBAM) with adversarial learning. First, a network structure combining a CBAM and temporal convolutional network (CBAM-TCN) is designed. Then, a deep feature extraction network is constructed using CBAM-TCN. Finally, by incorporating Domain Adversarial Neural Networks (DANN), the feature extraction network is optimized to enhance the cross-domain invariance and trend of deep features. The prediction accuracy of the proposed RUL prediction method is validated through multiple cross-condition RUL prediction tasks, demonstrating superior performance compared to other RUL prediction methods.

articleTitle: Analysis of Biosignal Data and Development of Estimation Systems for Artificial Insemination Timing of Cows
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an estimation system for Artificial Insemination (AI) timing based on analysis of the normal fluctuations for the body surface temperature (ST) of cows. Firstly, ST data is normalized and an approximate waveform via the fundamental waveform synthesis method is generated. Next, a reconstructed waveform which remove circadian rhythms and the high frequency noise is calculated, and feature parameters are extracted from the obtained reconstructed waveform. Moreover, estimation system for AI timing is developed by utilizing Maha-lanobis squared distance. In this paper, the proposed estimation system is presented and its effectiveness is evaluated.

articleTitle: Towards the Summary Depiction of Prevailing Power Flow Directionality Using A Wind Rose Representation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Effective visualisation of power grid data is critical for real-time monitoring and decision-making, particularly as grids become more complex with microgeneration and distributed energy resources. Traditional one-line diagrams of systems based on geographic representations can become unwieldy and challenging to interpret for large-scale grids. These diagrams are not designed to rapidly convey an at-a-glance indication of the overall prevailing directionality of power flow in all the lines making up a grid. This paper proposes two novel graphical devices to address these limitations: the PowerQuiver and the PowerRose. The PowerQuiver abstracts directional power flows in individual lines as oriented vectors emerging from the origin. This compactly depicts the magnitude and orientation of MW flows for an entire grid. The PowerRose simplifies this further by binning the power flows into directional segments, akin to a wind rose graphic. This allows for a neat and intuitive depiction of the overall directionality of prevailing power flows across a grid. These techniques aim to enhance traditional tools, offering more rapid summary views of power flow directionality that may support faster and better decision-making, potentially as auxiliary displays in control rooms.

articleTitle: Vehicle Front Lighting Instruction for Safety Driving on Nighttime Mountain Roads: From a Vehicle Control Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Ensuring driving safety on mountain roads at night is highly challenging due to limited visibility and the complex road conditions characterized by sharp curves. To address this issue, this paper presents a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework that integrates vehicle trajectory tracking with adaptive headlight control. The proposed method aims to optimize both vehicle driving behaviors and headlight illumination by adjusting the vehicle front lighting angle and distance, thereby maximizing visibility of the upcoming path while maintaining precise trajectory adherence. Several evaluation metrics are introduced to comprehensively assess the effectiveness of the approach. Simulation results on an S-shaped mountain road demonstrate that the proposed method not only achieves accurate trajectory tracking with reduced lateral errors but also ensures adequate lighting coverage, enhancing overall driving safety.

articleTitle: An Experimental Investigation Towards Optimization of Automatic Parameter Setting System for LCD 3D Printer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In recent years, as the price of 3D printers has dropped, they have become more accessible not only for industrial purposes but also for personal purposes, such as prototyping, making laboratory equipment, and use in junior high schools in Japan. The modeling methods used for low-cost models are fused deposition modeling (FDM) or Liquid Crystal Display (LCD), a type of stereolithography. Both have their own advantages, and LCD is superior to FDM in that it is capable of producing fine, smooth models and tends to reduce the modeling time when creating multiple items at once. However, LCD method is heavily influenced by the arrangement, orientation and the setting of parameters during the creation process. If the settings are not sufficiently considered, the possibility of modeling failure increases, which is a problem. The purpose of this research is to clarify the relationship between fabrication accuracy and the arrangement of a model in relation to the platform, orientation and parameter setting. In the experiment, objects were fabricated while varying the angle between the platform and the surface of the 3D model, exposure time, and layer pitch. Additionally, cube and oblique prism models were used to examine the effects of overhang. The flatness of each support-added surface and the straightness of each side were measured using an image dimension measuring device, and compared and evaluated for each condition. As a result, it was found that the presence of overhang significantly increases the likelihood of fabrication failure. Furthermore, increasing the angle between the platform and the model surface improves the accuracy of the surface where supports are attached.

articleTitle: Determination of Foster Model Parameters of Heatsink for High-Current Thyristor Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Thyristor-based power electronic converters have manifested and proved their performance and reliability in high-current applications for decades. These converters are an inevitable part in industry for challenging applications where the desired load characteristics have to be provided. Some traditional and common instances for their usage are in the traction power, excitation system of large power drives, compensation in grid, steel industry and many more. The high power handling capability of these converters comes with the cost of huge conduction losses in terms of heat. To keep the thyristors operating within their safe operating area, proper dimensioning of cooling system is required. Water-cooling for this type of converters is a common practice in the industry. This paper deals with the calculation of heatsink parameters for Forster model in such an application. Measured data from high current test are used to find the analytical model of the heatsink and then determined parameters are used in a computer simulation to validate the values. The used parameters from extracted model shows a good compliance with the measured temperature. Understanding the methodology, the performance of newly designed heatsinks can be estimated.

articleTitle: Semantic Model for the Description of Energy Data in the Module Type Package
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Modular production systems that employ the Module Type Package (MTP) to describe module interfaces can, at present, only communicate energy data through proprietary solutions. Due to this limitation, users face additional effort when calculating energy KPIs for modules or determining the energy efficiency of modules. To address this issue, we present a model that facilitates energy data to be described semantically and uniformly in the MTP on the basis of an industrial standard (OPC 34100). MTPs incorporating this model can transmit semantically consistent energy data from modules to the process control system, making the data available for further applications, such as monitoring or optimization.

articleTitle: Control of Active Parallel Filters with Selective Harmonic Compensation to Reduce Switching Power Losses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Harmonics generated by non-linear loads must be avoided to increase the overall quality of the power supply of power grids and microgrids. In this context, studies have been developed to improve the performance of active power filters. This work develops a control scheme for active filters composed of two Voltage Source Inverters that share the harmonics to be controlled. One of the inverters works at low frequency and controls the reactive power and the low order harmonics. Other inverter works at a high switching frequency and controls the high frequency harmonics. This inverter handles most of the harmonics, but its Root Mean Square (RMS) current is approximately 20% of the RMS current handled by the active power filter, so switching losses are significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Classical AC/DC Rectifiers for Hydrogen Electrolyzer Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This work compares six AC/DC power conversion chain topologies commonly employed by industrial companies for implementing electrolyzers. The main purpose is to help identify the eventual advantages of joining the traditional high-power rectifiers to an additional stage based on DC/DC conversion. The comparison is based on the current ripple, power factor, total harmonic distortion, scalability, and solution complexity. A Simulink model corresponding to each topology was developed to determine comparison criteria. The procedure consists of performing a steady-state analysis of each topology through simulations to obtain the main waveforms and the values of the established criteria and then calculating the scores for each technical solution. The findings indicated that the 24-pulse diode bridge rectifier plus DC-DC without interphase reactor exhibited the best performance.

articleTitle: Improved Data-Driven Trajectory Tracking Control for UMVs Under False Data Injection Attacks with a Time-Varying Step Size Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, the trajectory tracking problem of unmanned marine vehicles (UMVs) with false data injection (FDI) attacks is studied. Firstly, the dynamic linearization technique is used to convert the model of UMVs into equivalent data model. Secondly, to reduce tracking error during the update of the pseudo-Jacobian matrix (PJM) and control input, the step size factor is designed to be adjustable and time-varying. The radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) is used to compensate for the FDI attacks from the sensor to the controller side, so as to avoid negative effects on system control performance. The stability of the tracking error system is theoretically verified. Finally, the main results of this study are validated through simulations.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of Series Resonant Converter by Combined Frequency and Duty Ratio Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Resonant converters are widely used for voltage regulator applications. The basic converters i.e., Series resonant Converter (SRC) and Parallel Resonant Converter (PRC) are having some merits and limitations. These are addressed in multi element topologies at the cost of adding extra elements. This work takes up the SRC and reports a combined frequency and duty ratio control for performance optimization of the SRC. The key issue of SRC is that the voltage cannot be controlled at a low Q (i.e. Quality factor) operation. For example, at no load Q becomes zero making the converter inert to frequency variation. This however can be eliminated by pulse width modulation technique. Duty ratio can be properly controlled to achieve the output voltage at an extended load range. The work further takes up challenge to make efficiency optimized. For this a combined control of duty ratio and frequency are proposed. Efficiency Optimization Control (EOC) requires two voltage sensors (one at the input side and another at the output) and a current sensor. Following this, a new minimum rms current algorithm is developed that only requires a current and a voltage sensor. All the proposed techniques are simulated and verified using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Short-Term Forecasting of Thermostatic and Residential Loads Using Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) devices in smart grids enable intelligent energy management for grid managers and personalized energy services for consumers. Investigating a smart grid with IoT devices requires a simulation framework with IoT devices modeling. However, there lack comprehensive study on the modeling of IoT devices in smart grids. This paper investigates the IoT device modeling of a thermostatic load and implements the recurrent neural networks model for short-term load forecasting in this IoT-based thermostatic load. The recurrent neural network structure is leveraged to build a load forecasting model on temporal correlation. The temporal recurrent neural network layers including long short-term memory cells are employed to learn the data from both the simulation platform and New South Wales residential datasets. The simulation results are provided for demonstration.

articleTitle: Spatial-Temporal Fusion Deep Learning Model for Temperature and Relative Humidity Prediction in Multizone Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Accurate temperature and relative humidity predictions are important for efficient operation of HVAC systems. Current methods mostly ignore the correlation between two variables, which only achieve temperature prediction task, leading to insufficient information for single tasks. In addition, there is also a challenge of spatial coupling in multizone buildings. To solve these problems, we design a feature fusion multitask deep learning model, FFML, to predict temperature and relative humidity (RH) in multizone buildings. To address this challenge, we first extract the temporal and spatial features of these two variables. Subsequently, a transformer-based multitask deep learning model is designed to fuse these features and predict the values of two variables. In addition, auxiliary variables such as air conditioning (AC) power consumption are introduced into the framework to provide sufficient information. We conduct algorithm comparison experiment and ablation experiment using a public dataset. The results show that the proposed model is superior to existing methods for this task.

articleTitle: Design Procedure of a Brushless Induction Excited Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The Brushless Induction Excited Synchronous Generator (BINSYG) combines Synchronous and Induction Machines embedded in the same machine frame and wound for different numbers of poles to achieve magnetic decoupling. The machine is brushless and permanent magnet less. The Induction machine may be used in different modes to generate the required excitation current for the Synchronous Generator. In this work, the design procedure of the BINSYG (for both synchronous machine and induction machine) is explained, and a typical laboratory type, 5.5 kVA 415 V BINSYG is considered as an example. The designed machine is simulated in MAXWELL-2D, and the simulation results for no-load, isolated load, and grid-connected mode are shown.

articleTitle: Comparison of Several Variable Step Size Methods in the Optimization of Plug-and-Play Control for PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In complex industrial environments, motor operation is easily disturbed, leading to a decline in system performance. Traditional control methods typically require modifications to the existing controller structure when optimizing performance, whereas the advantage of Plug-and-Play (PnP) control lies in improving system performance by designing an auxiliary controller without altering the original controller. However, the traditional PnP control iterative optimization using constant step sizes often suffers from slow convergence. To this end, this paper studies and compares the application effects of various variable step-size methods in the design of the Q controller within the PnP structure, including Steepest Descent, Barzilai-Borwein, Adaptive Barzilai-Borwein, Gradient Scaling, and Fully Adaptive Nonlinear Normalized Gradient Descent. The effects of these variable step-size methods were validated through simulation experiments. The results show the effectiveness of variable step-size methods in improving controller convergence speed and system performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Feature Parameters and Their Time-Transition for Shockable Arrhythmia and Prediction of the Effect of Electrical Defibrillation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a prediction system of the effect of electrical defibrillation. In order to develop the proposed system, we firstly analyze from pre-shock (immediately before defibrillation) ECGs (ElectroCardioGrams) by using Gabor Wavelet Transform, Poincaré plot analysis, Spectral entropy, and feature parameters are extracted by those extracted analysis results, we focus on time-transition feature parameter. Next, effective feature parameters are selected based on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi^{2}$</tex> -test. Finally, “Effective” and “Ineffective” for electrical defibrillation are classified by using SVM (Support Vector Machine) with three kernels (Linear, Gaussian, and Polynomial) and regularization. In this way, we shows the effectiveness of the proposed feature extraction methods and prediction system.

articleTitle: Design and Test of a Scrolling LED Matrix Display Controlled by the Prevailing Speed of Transverse Motion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, a new concept and an initial prototype for a roaming light display is described. This device can display a light pattern that appears to be fixed in space, independent of the motion of the display. This illusion is achieved by scrolling the pattern backwards along the display at precisely the same speed at which the device is moving forward. Applications for such a device could include creating a virtual shoreline for maritime use, to allow ship passengers to visualise their speed in a situation where other points of reference are absent. The prototype described here uses a modified consumer grade Light Emitting Diode matrix, a Global Navigation Satellite System receiver as the method of determining velocity, and a microcontroller. The prototype demonstrates that such a device can display arbitrary text or graphic patterns fixed in the air as the device is moved along.

articleTitle: Characterization of Limit Cycles in Symmetric-Send-on-Delta Based Control Systems. A Describing Function Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper we study the limit cycles that may appear in closed loop PID control systems with symmetric send on delta sampling schemes. The analysis is based on the describing function (DF) technique. The DF of the Symmetric-Send-on-Delta sampler is obtained, leading to a plot that is formed by several lines, each one corresponding to a number of output level crossings of the output during the oscillation. The intersection of those lines with the open loop Nyquist plot of the system allows to predict the existence of limit cycles, their stability and the frequency and amplitude of oscillations. As the DF plot has several lines, several intersections may occur, and then several stable limit cycles are possible. Some examples have been presented with one, two and three different limit cycles to validate the limit cycle prediction strategy proposed.

articleTitle: VFD-Induced Harmonic Analysis and Performance Metrics of Multiphase Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Induction motors are pivotal in a variety of industrial applications, making their control a subject of crucial importance. Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) have gained prominence for their ability to efficiently modulate motor speed and torque according to load demands. Although VFDs offer considerable advantages in power efficiency and control precision, they also introduce harmonics into electrical systems due to the inherent nature of power electronic switching. This study specifically focuses on the impact of VFD-induced harmonics on the performance metrics of Squirrel Cage Induction Motors (SCIMs). Using MATLAB/SIMULINK for simulation, the paper conducts a comprehensive harmonic analysis to evaluate its effects on critical parameters such as speed and torque. The aim is to balance the benefits of VFDs with the challenges posed by harmonic distortions. The findings offer actionable information on optimizing VFD-based control strategies for multiphase induction motors. Therefore, the study contributes significantly to the ongoing discourse on harmonics management in complex motor drive systems.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Modulation Strategy for Neutral-Point Voltage Balancing Control and Common-Mode Voltage Suppression in Three-Level Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Taking the T-type three-level inverter as an example, this paper first analyzes the mechanisms behind the generation of common-mode (CM) voltage and neutral-point (NP) voltage in T-type three-level inverters. Next, it examines the CMR-VSVPWM (Common-mode Reduced Virtual Space Vector PWM) method, which can control NP voltage balance and suppress CM voltage based on SVPWM. To reduce the switching losses of CMR-VSVPWM while maintaining cons-istent fundamental voltage amplitude, the paper proposes the Space Vector DPWMA and a hybrid modulation strategy, HPWM. This strategy determines whether to switch the modulation strategy in the next switching cycle based on the NP voltage and the charge flowing through the neutral point. This enables control of NP voltage and suppression of CM voltage across the entire modulation index. Finally, the correctness and feasibility of the proposed modulation strategies are validated through simulations.

articleTitle: YOLOv8-FA: Multimodal Fusion Image Object Detection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: To address the issues of weak information expression capability of single-modal images and the limited receptive field of traditional object detection algorithms, we propose the YOLOv8-FA algorithm based on the YOLOv8 algorithm. In the backbone feature extraction network, the FasterNetBlock module is introduced to reduce the redundancy of model feature channels. Additionally, a depthwise separable convolution module is incorporated to enhance the receptive field of the network model's feature extraction. The loss function is improved to WIou to enhance the network's adaptive adjustment capability to the quality of input images. The training dataset is obtained by fusing visible light and infrared images based on the LLVIP dataset. Subjective and objective experimental results indicate that the proposed algorithm effectively improves the model's detection performance, reduces false detections and missed detections, and achieves object detection tasks in multimodal fused images.

articleTitle: Adaptive Gain Robust Preview Controllers for Uncertain Linear Discrete-Time Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper deals with a design method of adaptive robust preview controllers for uncertain linear discrete-time systems. The proposed control law consists of a state feedback term, an integral one, a preview input and a compensation input with adjustable parameters. In this paper, we show that sufficient conditions for the existence of the proposed adaptive robust preview controllers are given in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Finally, a numerical example is presented to demonstrate the effective of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Resource Efficient Path Planning for Mobile Manipulators in Recurring Machine Tending Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Mobile Manipulators are on the path to becoming a general purpose automation solution with applications in fields of manufacturing, healthcare among others. However, the potential of mobile manipulators for high mix - low volume production is not exhausted, with operation to be expected more time-efficient, resilient and most of all more flexible. This paper presents an approach to mobile manipulator path planning for servicing tasks in a factory environment. The proposed algorithm enables time-efficient manipulator motion planning for recurring pick-and-place tasks through online path planning that is guided by offline-generated support data. This leverages the existing redundancy of information between recurring service tasks and reduces the overall computation needed. The results show that this approach is faster than sampling-based planning in static environments and produces comparably short trajectories in static environments with collisions created through human error.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Resilient Sliding Mode Control of UMVs Subject to FDI Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this article, we address the problem of robust fixed-time stabilization for unmanned marine vehicles (UMVs) subject to false data injection (FDI) attacks and disturbances. First, an improved fixed-time sliding mode disturbance observer (FTSMDO) is proposed to enhance convergence speed and estimate external disturbances and attacks. Subsequently, a robust sliding mode control strategy is developed to ensure that system errors converge to a small neighborhood of the origin within a fixed time, even under FDI attacks, demonstrating improved convergence performance compared to existing methods. Finally, simulations demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively achieves stabilization and ensures the safety and robustness of the UMVs.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Network Based Disturbance Estimation Method for Stabilization Loop of Inertial Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The disturbance in the stabilization loop of the inertial platform seriously affects the system accuracy and performance. Conventional methods face challenges in identifying external disturbances. In this paper, a hybrid neural network based disturbance estimation method for inertial platform stabilization loop is proposed. The hybrid neural network model comprises a recurrent neural network (RNN) responsible for extracting local high-level disturbance features from time series, and gated recurrent units (GRU) used to compensate for global high-level disturbance features. Subsequently, these high-level features are fused and input into a fully connected layer for disturbance estimation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through the stabilization loop data from the inertial platform.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Integral Sliding Mode Optimal Control of the Linear Systems with Uncertainties Based on LQR Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents an event-triggered integral sliding mode control (EISMC) scheme aimed at solving the optimal control problem in linear systems. Initially, a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) controller is developed to achieve optimal control. Subsequently, we propose the EISM controller, which effectively addresses disturbances and system uncertainties while ensuring that the system remains in an optimal control state at all times. The EISM controller enhances both control accuracy and the frequency of updates, significantly reducing energy consumption. Additionally, we establish a lower bound for the event-triggered time interval to prevent zero behavior. Finally, we illustrate the effectiveness of our approach through simulation examples.

articleTitle: Dynamic Event-Triggered Fixed-Time Consensus Analysis of Multi-Agent Systems Under Input Delays and Switching Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic event-triggered control method for first-order multi-agent systems with input delays and disturbances under switching topologies. The controller design and its properties of dynamic event-triggered fixed-time consensus are presented in detail. Furthermore, agents can achieve consensus in a fixed time for any initial conditions and topologies that comply with the control protocol. Zeno behavior is avoided. Simulation examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and simulate scenarios in which the communication environment deteriorates due to external disturbances affecting the MASs.

articleTitle: A Distributed Algorithm for Solving Time-Varying Linear Equations based on the Newton Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This study introduces a distributed algorithm based on the Newton methods, which is designed to collaboratively solve time-varying linear equations with a unique solution through the cooperation of multiple agents. Each agent possesses only a portion of the global equation's information, specifically, a subset of the rows of the augmented matrix. Through communication among agents, the algorithm converges towards the global solution. When the derivative of the global solution of the time-varying equations is bounded, the algorithm ensures that the local solutions converge within a certain range of the global solution, thereby achieving tracking. The algorithm is also capable of rapidly solving time-invariant linear equations, quickly reaching consensus and determining the global solution of the equations. Efficacy and efficiency of the algorithm have been substantiated through a simulation experiment.

articleTitle: Geometric Attacks on a Color Quantum Image Watermarking Protocol Based on the LSB Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Research on quantum image watermarking protocols in terms of resistance to geometric attacks is relatively scarce. Therefore, it is crucial to delve into the study of geometric attack methods for quantum watermarking protocols.This paper investigates the robustness of quantum image watermarking protocols under geometric attacks. It explores various geometric attack techniques, including translation, flipping, shearing, and rotation.This paper does the simulation experiments for the protocol. The result shows that the protocol maintains recognizable watermark contours under translation, rotation, and flipping attacks. However, the details are distorted.In the case of shearing attacks, the watermark image becomes severely distorted. This proves that the protocol is not effective in resisting such geometric attacks, especially shearing attacks.

articleTitle: Sample-Based Modeling of Headlight Illumination Area Considering Combined Vehicle Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper focus on the modeling problem of the headlight illumination area, with a combination of vehicle dynamics, which is crucial for enhancing nighttime driving safety through intelligent headlight systems. The study addresses the limitations of existing models that oversimplify the illumination area and do not account for the irregular blind spots caused by brightness decay. The proposed model integrates vehicle pitch and roll movements with geometric analysis of light paths to provide a more accurate representation of the illumination area. It offers two control degrees of freedom for headlight pitch and yaw to feedback the illumination area, which is essential for control. The proposed model is verified through sampling methods and experimental data, demonstrating its effectiveness in characterizing the illumination area and its potential for realtime application in Intelligent vehicle lighting systems.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Stabilization of Linear Discrete-Time Stochastic Systems with Limited Data Rate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper considers the control problem of a class of linear discrete-time stochastic systems under a limited data rate. A quantized state-feedback control protocol is proposed, incorporating a random polar coordinate quantizer, a dynamic encoding-decoding scheme, and a controller design to achieve asymptotic stabilization of the closed-loop system in probability. A simulation example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed quantized state-feedback control protocol under the given data rate constraints.

articleTitle: Optimal Integral-Derivative Time Ratio for Tuning PID with Derivative Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes several strategies to fix the integral-derivative ratio to simplify the tuning of PID controllers with derivative filter, when an optimization of the performance with a constraint in the robustness is used. Fixing the integral-derivative ratio allows to reduce the computational complexity, as the search space is reduced. One classical proposal is to fix integral-derivative ratio to 4. We propose two new alternatives that improve the result of the optimization without increasing the computational cost.

articleTitle: A Robust Dynamic Output Feedback Control with Adaptive Compensation Inputs for a Class of Uncertain Switched Linear Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a design method of robust dynamic output feedback controllers for a class of uncertain switched linear systems. The proposed controller consists of a switching rule, a dynamic output feedback controller with an adaptive compensation input, and the adaptive compensation input is tuned by updating laws. In this paper, we show that sufficient conditions for the existence of the proposed robust output feedback control system are given in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs).

articleTitle: A Six-Degree-of-Freedom Global Optimization Method for Bidirectional Series Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The Dual Bridge Series Resonant Converter (DBSRC) under traditional single phase shift control is very easy to lose soft switching under light load and non-unit voltage gain, and has a large resonant current, which seriously affects the efficiency of the converter.
