To solve this problem, this paper proposes a 6-Degree-of-Freedom(6-DOF) global optimization control based on asymmetric phase shift, which can enable DBSRC to operate with zero return power and minimum resonant current while ensuring soft switching of all switching devices, thereby improving the efficiency of the converter. Finally, the feasibility and correctness of the proposed control strategy are verified by simulation, and the superiority of this control method in terms of resonant current and soft switching range is demonstrated by comprehensive comparison with SPS control, MCT control and M-MCT control.

articleTitle: Circulatory Failure Prediction by Using Wavelet Transform and Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In order to predict the circulatory failure ahead, a method is proposed by combing wavelet transform and machine learning methods AdaBoost, XGBoost, KNN and SVM. Wavelet transform can decompose the original time series into smooth and detail information on different resolution levels, which can detect the autoregression effect involved in the time series that can not be detected by these methods directly. By applying the method to a ICU dataset which contains 1718 patients and 18 variables, the results show that the methods AdaBoost and XGBoost gain good performance with ROC score around 0.96 when the time series is predicted ahead by 5 minutes, 25 minutes or 50 minutes. For patients under different basic clinical information, results show that age play an important role in model performance improvement, followed by sex, weight and height.

articleTitle: Reversible Data Hiding Using Dynamic Payload Truncation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The rapid development of technology has had a significant impact on communication and data exchange, leading to an increase in data theft. Confidential and private data is particularly vulnerable to hackers' theft and manipulation. Therefore, it is crucial to prioritize personal data protection in this digital era. One method to address this issue is steganography, which involves embedding secret messages into media such as audio samples. However, the development of steganography has revealed areas for improvement, such as a decline in stego-audio quality, represented by PSNR, which can result in the inability to retrieve the message. To address this issue, the linear interpolation method and payload truncation are utilized to minimize payload capacity in the audio sample insertion process. This ensures that each interpolated sample has a high capacity and quality for payload insertion.

articleTitle: Generalized Discontinuous and Pseudo-Discontinuous High-Speed Vibration-Damping Transfer Cam Curve with Arbitrary Rise Time Consisting of Half-Odd-Integer Trigonometric Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this study, we discuss a cam function with discontinuous displacement that enables vibration-damping transfer of an undamped 1DOF oscillator with any rise time. We derived this cam function from the solution of a two-point boundary value problem for a 1DOF oscillator with an enforced displacement of the root, consisting of half-odd integer trigonometric functions. By taking a linear combination of these functions, we can obtain a general solution for the cam function that meets the above conditions. Alternatively, we can obtain a pseudo-discontinuous cam function that is continuous but has abrupt changes in displacement by increasing the convergence value of the sum of the coefficients in an infinite series of continuous vibration-damped transfer cams. In the limit where the sum of the coefficients diverges, we can transform it into a discontinuous cam function.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Stator High Resistance Connection Based on Multiple Reference Frame Controllers in Asymmetrical Six-Phase AC PMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Increasing interest has been shown in multiphase drives for medium and high-power industrial applications, owing to their specific advantages when compared to their three-phase counterparts. High-resistance connections cause stator resistance unbalance, leading to a degraded performance of the machine, which in turn affects the efficiency and reliability of the machine and the overall system. In this paper, an improved field-oriented control scheme is designed to detect stator high-resistance connections, localize the affected phase/phase, and compensate the effect of the stator fault in order to keep the drive behavior nearly unchanged until a safe procedure to stop the drive is activated. The proposed control strategy is based on an analytical model that takes into account the stator resistance unbalance introduced by a high resistance connection, exploiting the control signals derived from multi-reference frame current regulators. The theoretical analysis of the diagnosis approach and the corresponding fault-tolerant control strategy are fully tested by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Solar-Rechargeable Remotely Controlled Boat Drone for River Bathymetry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This study focuses on designing a bathymetric boat drone and analyzing its findings. An airboat design is suitable for low maintenance and is equipped with a wireless receiver, proprietary controller, and a solar panel for charging. The study aims to identify differences in the riverbed using historical and collected data on Marikina and Jones Bridge. Bathymetric data is collected by the water level pressure, which is sent through Excel sheets and calculated using the hydrostatic pressure formula to get its height. Bathymetric data is only gathered in specific areas, thus having limited data that could help scientists and the government. Further exploration of this approach could yield valuable insights for governmental applications. The comparison showed an 11% error for the Marikina Bridge and a 27% error for the Jones Bridge. The T-test revealed a non-significant difference between the data, with a P-value of 0.14 for the Marikina Bridge and 0. 11 for the Jones Bridge. The average speed was 0.21 m/s for Marikina and 0.14 m/s for Jones Bridge.

articleTitle: Reachable Set Estimation for Multi-rate Sampled-data Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper broadens the scope of reachable set estimation (RSE) for multi-rate sampled-data (MRSD) systems with aperiodic sampled-data intervals affected by unit peak bounded disturbance (UPBD). Initially, a loop-based Lyapunov function (LBLF) is constructed to derive sufficient conditions that ensure all system states are confined within an ellipsoid. Following this, a MRSD controller is designed incorporating RSE, ensuring that the reachable sets of the system are contained within the specified target ellipsoid. A state feedback solution to the MRSD control problem is derived, utilizing LMI optimization alongside multi-rate control strategies. Lastly, the practical application demonstrates the effectiveness of the methodologies proposed in this study.

articleTitle: Distributed Learning Model Predictive Control with Coupled Constraints and Communication Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel distributed learning model predictive control (DLMPC) scheme for linear systems with coupled constraints under communication noise. In contrast to conventional distributed MPC schemes, the proposed scheme combines data-driven learning techniques with a novel noisy alternating direction multiplier method (NADMM). By learning from previous iterative trajectories, the proposed scheme enhances performance over time. Additionally, it addresses coupling constraint problem between subsystems and mitigates the impact of communication noise. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified through a simulation example.

articleTitle: Obstacle Detection Method Based on Fusion of Visual and Millimeter-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The fusion scheme of millimeter-wave radar(MMW radar) and visual sensors combines the characteristics of strong penetration and immunity to lighting interference from MMW radar, as well as the high resolution and robust recognition capabilities of cameras, enabling accurate perception and identification of obstacles, thereby significantly enhancing the adaptability of autonomous driving systems in complex weather conditions and road scenarios. This paper presents an obstacle detection method based on the fusion of visual and MMW radar information. This method replace the traditional Region Proposal Network(RPN) in the Faster R-CNN framework with the approach that utilizes high-precision target distance and velocity information from MMW radar to generate multi-scale candidate bounding boxes. By training and testing the network model of the fusion algorithm using the nuScenes dataset, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are validated, showcasing its robust adaptability in complex environments.

articleTitle: A New Pulse Skipping Control for Series Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a pulse skipping based combined frequency and duty ratio control for a series resonant converter which is targeted for voltage regulator applications. The proposed pulse skipping control combines duty ratio based phase shifted control for maintaining output voltage at its reference value, along with frequency based control which assists in development of the pulse skipping algorithm. This algorithm is structured so that pulses are skipped in generated gate pulses for upper switching devices present in the converter whenever the output voltage tries to be higher than its specified maximum value or be lower than its specified minimum value. These maximum and minimum voltages are determined based on its reference voltage and allowable voltage ripple within which the oscillations in output voltage are desired to be in. The converter system with the proposed control method is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment to validate its performance under transient conditions e.g., variation in load resistance and output voltage reference. The system performance with proposed method is also compared with conventional method where the proposed control demonstrates its superiority by significantly minimizing the output voltage ripple.

Author Keywords: duty ratio based phase shifted control

articleTitle: Fault Visualization: Enhancing Learning in Power Electronics Using Industrial Evidence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Understanding faults in electrical boards is of great importance in industry. Generally, recognizing and managing faults in electrical boards plays a key role in maintaining safety, reducing costs, and increasing efficiency across various industries. To familiarize with common faults in electrical boards, this article presents a creative method for teaching some of these faults. The proposed method uses real images of common faults in electrical boards and engages students in important concepts related to faults. This approach helps students gain a better understanding of scientific concepts through real images. Additionally, it enables students to effectively apply their theoretical knowledge in their professional practices. A quantitative analysis of the results demonstrates the effectiveness and satisfaction of students with the proposed method.

articleTitle: AVP Prediction Research Based on Generative Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Antiviral peptides (AVPs) are short molecules that inhibit viral replication and spread, offering potential for treating infections and supporting the development of antiviral drugs and vaccines. However, the limited availability of natural AVP data, due to difficulties in acquiring and culturing specific viral strains, hinders the statistical reliability of AVP studies. This limitation impacts the identification and analysis of AVPs' effects and mechanisms. To address this challenge, this research introduces a data augmentation method based on generative networks for AVP prediction. The method includes three modules: generation, screening, and validation. The generation module employs a WGAN-based generative network to synthesize AVPs. The screening module applies the Meta-iAVP classifier to filter the synthesized sequences, and the validation module utilizes a two-layer GRU classifier to validate the augmented AVP data. Experimental results demonstrate that increasing the amount of synthetic AVP data enhances the classifier's Area Under the Curve (AUC) value, confirming the effectiveness of AVP data augmentation for classification tasks. This generative network-based approach to AVP data augmentation shows great potential for discovering new antiviral peptides and exploring innovative antiviral drugs.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Image Steganography Using Pixel Differencing for Better Data Hiding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Securing confidential information over communication channels is critical in today's data transmission era. Steganography, a data protection technique, enables covert communication. However, many existing steganographic algorithms face challenges in balancing the hidden data size with the quality of the carrier image after embedding. This paper presents a novel steganographic method that employs pixel value differencing to address these challenges more effectively. The proposed approach enhances neighboring pixel optimization, allowing for data concealment with high imperceptibility. Experimental results demonstrate strong carrier image quality, with Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) values ranging from 45.453 to 62.362 dB and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) values between 0.990 and 0.999. This method significantly outperforms existing techniques, establishing it as a cutting-edge solution.

articleTitle: Closed-Loop Control of GaN-HEMT-Based Buck Converter Using Modified RGDC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper explores a resonant gate driver circuit (RGDC) with closed-loop control for Gallium Nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) in buck power conversion systems. Modern industries increasingly rely on high-frequency electronic devices, particularly Wide Bandgap (WBG) semiconductors like Silicon Carbide (SiC) and Gallium Nitride (GaN), for their superior characteristics over conventional silicon. The RGDC design aims to minimize gate power loss during high-frequency operation, enhancing overall performance. Simulations validate the effectiveness of the approach, showcasing improved voltage stability, reduced overshoot, and enhanced regulation compared to open-loop control. The closed-loop scheme dynamically adjusts and maintains desired output levels, leading to enhanced performance, stability, and reliability in GaN HEMT-based converters.

articleTitle: Dynamic Jumps of an Agile Bicycle Through Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Controlling bicycles during dynamic maneuvers, such as jumps, poses significant challenges due to the intricate demands of balance and stability. This study utilizes the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm to control both ground navigation and dynamic jumps. Stability on flat terrain is maintained through steering adjustments, while jumps are facilitated by vertical thrust. The proposed approach is validated through simulation, showing high success rates in jump execution, along with improved balance and adaptability. These results underscore the potential of reinforcement learning-based control systems in managing complex dynamic movements and contribute to the development of more robust motion control strategies for bicycles on both structured and unstructured terrains. The attached video is given in https:/lingi-ye.github.io/video/flybike.mp4.

articleTitle: Biological Data Analysis Based on Envelopes for Estimation of Calving Phase of Cows
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, for the purpose of development of a discrimination system based on the normal phase of body surface temperature (ST) data of cows, we show analysis results of ST data. For analysis of ST data, we firstly extract objected waveforms from ST data, and outlier in the extracted data is removed. Next, approximate waveforms based on Fourier series expansion are generated, and their envelopes are calculated. Furthermore, feature parameters are extracted from envelopes. Finally, we discuss effective feature parameters for the discrimination system.

articleTitle: Analysis of Body Surface Temperature Data of Cows Based on the Continuous Wavelet Transform with Pseudo-Differential Operators for Detection of Optimal AI Timing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the body surface temperature (ST) data of cows for the purpose of estimating the optimal artificial insemination (AI) timing. Firstly, outliers in the ST data are removed. next, the approximate waveform is generated by using the fundamental waveform synthesis based on Fourier series expansion. Moreover the reconstructed waveform is also calculated. In the reconstructed waveform, the effect of circadian rhythm is suppressed by calculating the differences between the average values at the same time over the last three days. Furthermore, the continuous wavelet transform with pseudo- differential operator is applied to the reconstructed waveform, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{NSI}^\alpha$</tex> is derived from the resulting scalogram. Finally, the features attributed to ovulation in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{NSI}^{\alpha}$</tex> are compared and analyzed.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Dual Active Bridge Converter Using Planar Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The integration of planar printed circuit board (PCB) transformer into the DAB converter architecture offers a effective option for high-frequency isolated power conversion. This work examines the use of planar transformers in the DAB architecture, providing advantages such as decreased size and improved power density. This paper presents the operational principles of the DAB converter using planar transformers and discusses important design considerations. Simulation studies using MATLAB software and experimental validation using the developed hardware prototype are carried out and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Enhancement vs Cascode Gallium Nitride MOSFET: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Wide band gap semiconductor device i.e. Gallium Nitride (GaN) MOSFET is widely employed in high power density applications due to the excellent switching characteristics and lower on-state conduction losses as compared to the Si devices. Utilizing WBG devices for higher switching frequency application, the analysis of the turn-on and turn-off switching energy losses and reverse recovery loss is of paramount importance for the thermal design. In this study, an analysis on the switching energy loss, reverse-recovery charge and reverse-recovery time for cascode and enhancement configurations of GaN MOSFET has been performed using LTspice software. The effect of gate parasitic inductance on the gate-voltage of both configurations has also been analyzed. The obtained simulation results show that e-GaN offers the lower losses as compared to cascode-GaN MOSFET. Further, the gate voltage of the e-GaN MOSFET is less noise immune for the parasitic inductance.

articleTitle: Collaborative Conditional Anti-Windup - Case of Field Oriented Control of Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Cascaded control loops simplify managing complex control systems by structuring multiple control loops in a hierarchical manner, where the bounded output of one loop serves as a setpoint for another. Through cascading, each loop can be independently tuned, optimizing control for specific subsystem dynamics. This paper introduces a new method enabling collaborative functionality among the anti-windup mechanism of controllers within a cascaded structure. By employing a new clamping anti-windup strategy, outer loops halt integration when inner loop saturates, circumventing superfluous error accumulation and enhancing system response. The proposed method is tested on a field oriented controller (FOC) for an induction machine undergoing abrupt changes in the DC link voltage. Simulation results show that the proposed anti-windup approach outperforms the conventional clamping anti-windup technique, particularly regardina the settling time for the motor speed.

articleTitle: Investigations on Static and Dynamic Current Sharing Performance in Paralleled GaN MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: GaN MOSFETs, known for their high electron mobility and low switching losses, are being increasingly used in power electronic systems. When GaN MOSFETs are operated in parallel, an imbalance in the current sharing can be observed, which could lead to reduced efficiency and potential device failure. This paper presents a comprehensive study of the current sharing in two GaN MOSFETs operating in parallel, with emphasis on the effects of mismatch in gate pulse synchronization. The imbalance in the current sharing is studied for various delays between the gate pulses, the corresponding nature of the current in both MOSFETs is analyzed, and relevant conclusions are drawn from it. This study conducted using LTspice simulation software provides insights for active gate driver development suitable for GaN MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Integrated Path Following and Adaptive Front-Light Control of Autonomous Vehicles: A Unified MPC Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents a co-design framework for autonomous vehicle path following and adaptive front-light control to enhance visibility and safety, particularly during complex maneuvers. This co-design approach utilizes a model predictive control method, where combined cost functions for path tracking and front-light angle adjustments are optimized simultaneously. A preview distance, D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf>, is designed to vary with vehicle speed and path curvature, providing anticipatory lighting control that minimizes blind spots and aligns with the vehicle's path-following requirements. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in maintaining accurate path tracking while providing optimal illumination under varying driving conditions, offering an integrative solution for autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Analysis of Biological Data Based on the $k$-Means Method for Development of Detection Systems for Calving Phase of Cows
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze body surface temperature data of cows for development the detection system for the calving phase. Firstly, we perform preprocess to remove the noise in the body surface temperature. Secondly, approximate waveforms based on Fourier series expansion are generated, and the frequency components which does not correspond to calving phase is removed. Next, by using the feature parameters obtained from the approximate waveform, the k-means method is applied to generate a cluster for the normal phase for each individual of cows. Then, we analyze the temperature characteristic based on the variation of feature parameters, and discuss the effectiveness of the detection system for calving phase.

articleTitle: Lessons from Deploying AAS Digital Twins for Factory Buildings with Papyrus4Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is one of the technological pillars forming Industry 4.0. It describes a scenario in which heterogeneous industrial devices at the operational technology (OT) layer, ranging from tiny sensors to massive fabrication equipment, are interconnected and collaborate to improve manufacturing's real-time monitoring and controlling. A smart factory built upon an IIoT framework is required to effectively organize the big data generated by such devices to feed artificial intelligence services at the information technology (IT) layer. Addressing this need, Asset Administration Shell (AAS) has recently emerged as a strong standard for representing resources at the OT layer with a standardized interface for all applications at the IT layer. This paper shares our experiences from a case study in developing AAS digital twins for factory buildings using the Papyrus4Manufacturing tool and model-driven engineering.

articleTitle: Phase Current Shape Factors for Fast-Robust OCF Detection and Localization in Multiphase DC-DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel fault detection and localization technique for open-circuit faults (OCF) in multiphase DC-DC converters using only the sensed variables from the control loops, eliminating the need for additional hardware. The proposed technique is based on the analysis of the phase current shape factors(PCSF) which are the derivatives (slope) of the inductor current for each phase. Additionally, it incorporates supplementary indicators to confirm the detected OCF. The proposed method is distinguished by fast detection capabilities and robustness against step changes in the duty cycle, load variations, parameter changes, and noise in the measurements. The effectiveness, rapidity, and robustness of the technique are validated through simulation tests on a four-phase DC-DC converter at different operating conditions.

articleTitle: Scheduling and Control of Ice-based Thermal Energy Storage HVAC Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Ice-based thermal energy storage air conditioning (TES-HVAC) can utilize different electricity prices to store ice at night and melt ice during the day, effectively reducing peak load on the power grid and saving costs. However, the commonly used fixed schedule, rule-based and model-based predictive control methods cannot effectively address issues such as uncertain cooling loads, and cannot achieve good cooling scheduling and air volume control. This article proposes a hierarchical ice-based thermal energy storage air conditioning scheduling optimization control method based on genetic algorithm (GA) and deep reinforcement learning (DRL). The upper layer uses GA to achieve cooling scheduling of energy storage air conditioning based on time of use electricity price and weather information, while the lower layer uses DRL method to achieve multi area air volume control. Compared with the fixed schedule strategy, the proposed method achieves a cost reduction of about 16.1%, while effectively improving thermal comfort.

articleTitle: Conversion of Industrial Robots to DC Power Supply: Efficiency, Protection Concepts and Recuperation Potential
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The confluence of high-quality standards and escalating wage costs is driving the adoption of automation in production facilities to unprecedented levels. This is made possible by the deployment of industrial robots and other technological solutions. In contrast to manual work, electric motor-driven robots require significantly more energy, which must be reduced in order to facilitate the energy transition and ensure the economic efficiency. Modern direct current (DC) grids possess the advantage of integrating renewable energies and storage in an efficient manner, and they can also supply consumer systems such as electric drives energy and material-efficient by eliminating unnecessary conversion processes due to their architectural design. Despite the considerable potential, high-performance DC grids are currently only in use in industry as test systems. Numerous products, standards and experience in planning and commissioning are still lacking for the roll-out. Grid participants are generally only supplied with an alternating current (AC) connection. The conversion of the power supply of a large six-axis industrial robot is demonstrated, in which a rectifier stage was removed and the necessary switching and protective devices for safe grid operation were installed. The energy requirement in DC operation was found to be reduced by a range of 1.12 % to 12.62 % in fast operation, based on the analysis of various movement patterns and loads. In slow operation, the higher base load in AC mode and the low utilisation of the power electronics result in significantly higher energy requirements, which in some cases exceed 50 %. Recuperation within the robot can already be used even in AC operation of the robot if several axes are moved simultaneously. However, energy exchange with other grid participants or intermediate storage in the grid storage units only works in the DC grid. This use of recuperation in the DC grid results in savings of up to 25.7 % in the field test if an entire ramp up and down process is considered. The study demonstrates the essential steps for a DC retrofit with regard to converting the energy supply of systems and how these can be integrated into a DC grid in a safe and compliant manner.

articleTitle: Day-Ahead Residential Load Forecasting based on Variational Mode Decomposition and Hybrid Deep Networks with Granger Causality Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Accurate forecast of residential load consumption enables utilities to make informed decisions that ensure a consistent power supply. Forecasting power usage, on the other hand, is difficult owing to the nonlinear and nonstationary characteristics of time series load data that is highly correlated with weather parameters. In order to solve this issue, the paper offers a variational mode decomposition (VMD) based load forecasting technique paired with a hybrid deep learning model integrating long short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU). VMD is a non-recursive signal processing approach that splits time series into band-limited modes referred to as intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). The IMFs are then predicted by the LSTM and GRU networks, and the results are merged to get the final forecast. The suggested model forecasts day-ahead load consumption with a resolution of 30 minutes. The results show that the VMD-LSTM-GRU model performs better than other tested recurrent models.

Author Keywords: Hybrid deep neural network for load forecasting

articleTitle: Enhancing Robotic Arm Path Planning Efficiency Through a Phased Reward Configuration Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of inefficiency and randomness in deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for robotic arm path planning and obstacle avoidance. To tackle these issues, we propose a Phased Reward Configuration Mechanism (PRCM), which divides the learning process into distinct phases. Each phase employs a customized reward function designed to optimize the robotic arm's movements in various operational regions, such as fast approach, stationary approach, and obstacle regions. By dynamically adjusting the reward based on the arm's position and task progress, PRCM guides more efficient exploration and improves path planning performance. We integrate this approach with several DRL algorithms and conduct simulation experiments to evaluate its effectiveness. The results show that PRCM significantly enhances the stability and efficiency of the training process, improving both the quality of path planning and the arm's ability to work in complex environments.

articleTitle: Memory Compact and Computationally Efficient Methods for Modeling Saturation in Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Synchronous machines are commonly used in power generation, electric propulsion, and industrial automation. Accurate modeling of these machines is essential, particularly in addressing challenges posed by nonlinear characteristics such as magnetic saturation. Traditional models often rely on computationally intensive methods to account for these nonlinearities, leading to slow simulations and high memory requirements. This paper introduces two new models: the enhanced explicit flux correction (EFC-2D) model, which captures magnetic saturation using two-dimensional lookup tables (2D-LUTs) with improved computational efficiency, and the single polynomial (S-POLY) model, which represents saturation using polynomials to significantly reduce memory usage. The proposed models are compared to the advanced one-dimensional explicit flux correct model (EFC-1D) and the model in Matlab/Simulink's Simscape Electrical Specialized Power Systems (SPS) toolbox. Simulation results, including both offline and real-time tests, show that EFC-2D and S-POLY models are computationally faster than conventional methods, with S-POLY being more memory-efficient than EFC-1D and EFC-2D models. These improvements make the proposed models ideal for high-performance simulations requiring both speed and memory optimization.

articleTitle: Real-Time Estimation of Grid Impedance and Voltage Using an Extended Kalman Filter in Natural Frame
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) based algorithm for real-time estimation of both grid impedance and the voltage amplitude in electrical networks. Operating directly in the natural frame, the method provides a more accurate representation of real systems subject to changing conditions, addressing limitations of traditional approaches that rely on synchronous of stationary frames. By continuously updating its estimates in real-time, the algorithm avoids the batch data processing common in many existing techniques. It also balances precision and computational complexity by choosing the appropriate variables to identify accounting for the nonlinear nature of the identification algorithm and by the addition of an internal resonator that tracks the unknown voltage. The proposed approach is particularly useful for networks with high penetration of renewable energy sources, where grid conditions can change rapidly, requiring the adaption of grid-connected converters to ensure the stability of the grid. A series of simulations have been conducted, and the initial results show good performance of the algorithm in estimating grid parameters under various dynamic conditions.

articleTitle: Improving Decision Accuracy and Safety of Autonomous Buses at Yellow-Light Intersections Through Integrated Decision-Making and eHMI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The integration of autonomous buses into urban transportation systems presents significant opportunities to reduce traffic congestion and improve road safety. However, the challenge of navigating yellow-light intersections, specifically the “dilemma zone”, remains a critical safety concern. This paper proposes an advanced system to address the decision-making and external communication requirements for autonomous buses operating at yellow-light intersections. Building on research in vehicle positioning and traffic signal detection, as well as the development of external human-machine interfaces (eHMI), this work introduces a hybrid system that enhances both the decision-making and communication with surrounding road users. The decision-making algorithm utilizes a camera-based recognition approach to accurately identify traffic signal transitions and the bus's positioning relative to the intersection, thereby optimizing stop-or-go decisions during the yellow-light phase. This is coupled with an eHMI system that dynamically displays the autonomous bus's intended actions (e.g., “Go Straight”, “Stop”) to external traffic participants, improving interaction and reducing ambiguity in mixed traffic environments. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed system, significantly reducing the risk of accidents in the dilemma zone while facilitating smoother integration of autonomous buses into urban traffic. The findings contribute to advancing intelligent public transportation systems and enhancing safety protocols for autonomous driving technologies.

articleTitle: Considering the Implications of Battery Aging in Multi-Year Capacity Expansion Planning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-year capacity expansion planning (CEP) model that implicitly accounts for batteries' degradation due to calendar and cycling aging. As the power system transitions towards higher renewable energy sources (RES) penetration, understanding the impact of battery degradation on long-term planning is crucial for reliable and cost-effective integration of energy storage solutions. The proposed model uses an iterative approach to dynamically estimate battery degradation, updating the state of charge (SoC) by incorporating degradation from the previous iteration. By employing the rainflow counting algorithm, the model accurately tracks capacity fade caused by cycling degradation, refining SoC until assumed degradation aligns with real operational conditions. The model also optimizes capacity decisions across multiple planning periods from 2030 to 2060. Results indicate that although the total system cost remains almost unaltered after several iterations, the optimal storage mix changes, with pumped-hydro facilities gradually replacing batteries. The study demonstrates the importance of capturing the long-term effects of battery storage degradation in multi-year CEP models. It also contributes to improving the CEP models' formulation and outcomes by capturing the expected dynamics between the required batteries and pumped-hydro storage capacities in the long run.

articleTitle: Disturbance Rejection Target Tracking Control for Snake Robots in the Presence of Obstacles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, a collision-free target tracking control approach utilizing guided vector field guidance is proposed. In particular, a synthesized vector field is designed to direct the snake robot toward the target while simultaneously navigating around multiple obstacles. In addition, a saturated guidance law is designed to compute a reference angular velocity to prevent damage to the robot joints. A dynamics control law is designed based on a reduced-order structure-modified expansion state observer to compensate for external disturbances and realize the robust target tracking and tracing control of the snake robot. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed guidance and control method.

articleTitle: Lyapunov-Based Distributed Model Predictive Control for Trajectory Tracking of USV with Fuzzy Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: A Lyapunov-based distributed model predictive control (LDMPC) scheme with fuzzy constraints is first developed for trajectory tracking of the unmanned surface vessel (USV), which is output-constrained and thrust-limited. The output of the fuzzy inference system is an interval instead of a value obtained by conventional defuzzification. The unnecessary overshoot of USV's states are reduced by fuzzy constraints. To guarantee stability, a contractive constraint based on Lyapunov function is further introduced. Although the addition of fuzzy constraints leads to an increase in computational complexity, embracing suboptimal solutions can help reduce the computational burden by using the Lyapunov constraint. Finally, numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed LDMPC scheme can guarantee the tracking performance with the smaller possible output.

articleTitle: Maximizing Economic Benefits in Distribution Networks by Optimizing Electric Vehicle Charging Stations and Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has posed significant challenges to distribution networks (DN), particularly regarding voltage stability and power losses. Integrating electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) with capacitors, which provide reactive power compensation, offers a solution to these challenges by enhancing voltage profiles, minimizing system losses, reducing total energy costs, and mitigating interruption costs. This study aims to optimize the net present value (NPV) by strategically reducing energy losses and expected interruption costs (EIC) through the optimal placement of capacitors in distribution systems. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is utilized to determine the most effective locations and capacities for EVCS and capacitors within the network. The impact of EVCS on NPV is also thoroughly analyzed to demonstrate their economic viability and overall network benefits. The proposed method is validated using the IEEE 10-bus system, showcasing its effectiveness in improving system performance and financial returns compared to traditional placement strategies.

articleTitle: Voltage Balancing and Energy Sorting of 17-Level Z Packed U-Cell MMC Using Real-Time Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) is a promising topology for medium-/high voltage applications due to its several features, mainly scalability, modularity, and reduced harmonics content. Yet, this complex topology faces several challenges in validating and verifying proposed control and modulation techniques due to its complex structure and difficulty in having a real prototype. Therefore, Real-Time (RT) simulation is an excellent alternative for verifying the operation of a MMC and its control while avoiding high-cost corrective methods. However, due to the excessive number of non-linear devices in MMC, which create additional computation burden, RT implementation of MMC becomes challenging as well. In this paper, a FPGA-based RT simulation is adopted for the implementation of a 17L-MMC based on Z Packed U-Cell Converter for its submodule, to verify the performance of voltage balancing and energy sorting algorithms, while obtaining efficient and accurate waveforms results.

articleTitle: Topology Planning for LEO Satellites Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite network has made significant advancements in global communication services, offering low latency and extensive coverage. Effective topology planning has the dual benefit of enhancing network Quality of Service and reducing signal delay, while simultaneously optimizing resource utilization. The advent of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methodologies offers novel approaches to inter-satellite topology planning in LEO constellations. In this work, a DRL topology planning algorithm based minimum spanning tree (DQN-MST) is proposed and compared with two traditional graph optimization algorithms. The results demonstrate that DQN-MST reduces the total network link length by 38.20% and 62.62% compared to the graph optimization algorithms, confirming the effectiveness of DQN-MST.

articleTitle: Remote Power Control and Monitoring of Cross-Platform Devices Using Magic Packets Across Network Boundaries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper compares online device discovery and remote startup and shutdown solutions for an enterprise network. As some of for these solutions do only work in a local network and the enterprise network consists of several subnetworks with different firewalls setting, a concept to communicate securely across subnetworks is required. For an evaluation, a prototype is implemented using Wake-on-Lan for startup, Address Resolution Protocol for online detection and Secure Shell for shutting down. Bridged MQTT-brokers are used to communicate across subnetwork with a service in every subnetwork. The central hosted prototype is able to switch on or off computers remotely in every subnetwork.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of Autonomous Surface Vehicles Using Fixed-Time Lyapunov-Based Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper aims to develop a novel fixed-time Lyapunov-based model predictive control (FTLMPC) scheme for the trajectory tracking control of autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) to improve the trajectory tracking performance. It is worth emphasizing that fixed-time control (FTC) is first emeging into the LMPC framework. By introducing the fixed-time auxiliary control system within the contraction constraints of Lyapunov-based model predictive control (LMPC) framework, the control performance of trajectory tracking is significantly improved, theoretically achieving fixed-time convergence. Mean-while, taking into account the practical constraints of the actuator thrusts, the input constraints are incorporated into the control strategy, explicitly defining a feasible attraction domain that ensures fixed-time stability. Simulation results validate that this method exhibits excellent control performance.

articleTitle: Optimizing Alarm Design: A Comparison of Delay-Timers, Counters, and Time-Deadbands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Alarm systems are crucial for ensuring the safety and efficiency of industrial operations. However, operators often face an overwhelming number of alarms, many of which are false or nuisance alarms. To address this issue and to enhance alarm system performance, techniques such as delay-timers, up/down counters, and time-deadbands are employed in alarm design. This paper provides a comprehensive comparative analysis of these techniques using performance indices, namely, False Alarm Rate (FAR), Missed Alarm Rate (MAR), and Expected Detection Delay (EDD). The study aims to identify the optimal technique yielding the best trade-off between accuracy and delay. The contributions of this paper are twofold: (1) A systematic performance analysis of the three techniques is conducted. This includes individual evaluations under varying alarm thresholds, accuracy comparisons using Receiver Operating Characteristics (ROC) curves, and a generalized comparison combining accuracy and delay. (2) A novel algorithm is proposed to select the optimal alarm reduction technique for a given detection delay, allowing operators to meet practical constraints in alarm system design efficiently. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through numerical examples, with results presented as augmented matrices and visualized through color-coded plots. This simultaneous comparison of techniques facilitates the design of more efficient and reliable alarm systems.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic, Emergency Auxiliary Communications, and Electronics (PEACE) Amateur Radio Station for Disaster Relief
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In the aftermath of natural disasters such as tornadoes or hurricanes, modern infrastructure-especially the electrical grid-often sustains significant damage, leading to widespread communication failures. Reliable communication systems are critical for effective disaster relief, yet the absence of power exacerbates these challenges for citizens, emergency services, and government entities. This paper presents a Photovoltaic Emergency Auxiliary Communications and Electronics (PEACE) Station, a portable solar-battery-powered solution designed to meet critical communication needs during emergencies. The PEACE station features a 100W solar panel array, a battery pack, a reconfigurable open-source power electronics converter, and an ICOM 2720 Transceiver for amateur radio communication. Field tests have been conducted to evaluate the system's performance, demonstrating its potential as a deployable solution in disaster relief operations.

articleTitle: Exploring LLMs for Verifying Technical System Specifications Against Requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Requirements engineering is a knowledge intensive process and crucial for the success of engineering projects. The field of knowledge-based requirements engineering (KBRE) aims to support engineers by providing knowledge to assist in the elicitation, validation, and management of system requirements. The advent of large language models (LLMs) opens new opportunities in the field of KBRE. This work experimentally investigates the potential of LLMs in requirements verification. Therein, LLMs are provided with a set of requirements and a textual system specification and are prompted to assess which requirements are fulfilled by the system specification. Different experimental variables such as system specification complexity, the number of requirements, and prompting strategies were analyzed. Formal rule-based systems serve as a benchmark to compare LLM performance to. Requirements and system specifications are derived from the smart-grid domain. Results show that advanced LLMs, like GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet, achieved f1-scores between 79 % and 94 % in identifying non-fulfilled requirements, indicating potential for LLMs to be leveraged for requirements verification.

articleTitle: Real-Time Monitoring and Trace Based on Nested COBS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Monitoring and tracing are integral to embedded systems development. In context of real-time systems, overhead is of essence as the timing behavior might be affected. In this paper we present Real-Time Monitor and Trace (RTMT) targeting (hard) real-time systems with static priority preemptive scheduling. Features of RTMT include both traditional logging capabilities, as well as event monitoring functionality. We show its feasibility to the Hippomenes FPGA implementation of the RISC-V RT architecture and demonstrate that cycle accurate time stamping of interrupt entry/exit and resource locking/unlocking is possible with zero interference to the running application. Logging, on the other hand comes with constant time overhead and is guaranteed to be non-blocking. RTMT builds on Nested COBS (N-COBS), a novel extension of the COBS protocol allowing for static priority preemptive framing with single byte overhead. In the paper we present the N-COBS protocol, formalize and prove its key properties: protocol soundness, encoder/decoder reversibility and single byte overhead. Design simplicity is demonstrated by the provided System Verilog encoder implementation as used to showcase monitoring and tracing of Rust RTIC applications running on the RISC-V RT architecture.

articleTitle: The Effects of Feature Selection and Balancing Dataset to Improve IoT-Based IDS Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The amount of data has increased dramatically over the past decade, which has made classifying the data more complicated, mainly when the data contains an uneven distribution, which indicates that one majority class has more instances than others. Standard classifiers can disregard the minority class entirely in this situation and have a tendency to classify all samples as belonging to the majority class. In the area of IDS study research, this imbalanced dataset is frequently found, as naturally, the amount of benign traffic outweighs the number of cyber threats. Researchers often implement the SMOTE technique for this challenge, particularly the over-sampling method. Nonetheless, other SMOTE techniques, namely undersampling and combined sampling, are rarely implemented. In this work, we attempt to balance the RT IoT 2022 dataset with wrapper feature selection and to-fold cross-validation. The result was then evaluated using several machine learning classifiers, including K-nearest neighbors, Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, and Adaptive Boosting. The result indicates that in terms of accuracy, Random Forest exceeds other classifiers in either oversampling, undersampling, or combined experiments at 99.09%, 98.65%, and 99.97%, respectively.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of Optimized PWM VSI-Driven Tri- and Pentaphase Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This study conducts an exhaustive comparative analysis of three-phase and five-phase induction motors, focusing on their performance when driven by a Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation Voltage Source Inverter (SPWM VSI). The objective is to elucidate the inherent strengths and limitations of each type of motor, using mathematical models grounded in electromagnetic principles. These models encompass critical parameters such as stator and rotor windings, magnetic field distribution, torque generation, and overall performance metrics. Through SPWM VSI, the paper examines aspects like total harmonic distortion (THD), waveform quality, and motor efficiency. A multi-faceted comparison is performed, emphasizing key performance indicators like torque production, speed variability, and harmonic content. The study also investigates the influence of additional phases in the five-phase motor on these performance parameters. The results obtained from the MATLAB/Simulink simulations are presented to support the comparative analysis. Overall, the findings offer nuanced insights into the suitability of tri- and pentaphase motors for diverse industrial applications, given their respective advantages and drawbacks.

articleTitle: An Assistance System for Simulation Model Adaptation and Parameter Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In the process industry, simulation models are a vital tool for enhancing decision-making by means of predictive analysis. Accurate model adaptation is crucial in order to maintain the reliability of simulation predictions and to account for changes in the real plant. The obstacle of non-uniqueness in parameter influences on variables complicates the adaptation process because it requires identifying which parameters have actually changed in the real plant, leading to potential ambiguity in parameter identification and estimation. This paper presents an assistance system for validating and adapting simulation model parameters, addressing non-uniqueness in parameter influences. Using Bayesian Optimization, it isolates parameter influences and adjusts parameters to minimize deviations between simulation model output and real data. An incorporation of expert knowledge ensures realistic parameter boundaries and prioritization for model adaptation, maintaining the model's predictive accuracy. The proposed system is validated on a laboratory scale process plant for the scenario of wear. Validation results demonstrate that the parameters changed in the real plant were accurately detected, leading to a successful model adaptation and reduced deviations.

articleTitle: Results on Using an Elevator with an Omnidirectional Mobile Robot in a Multi-Story Building
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Mobile robots operating in multi-story buildings require some way to effectively and reliably switch between floors. The existing elevator systems present in many buildings offer a relatively simple way to transport the robot to a new floor without the need for complex motion systems or specialized robot modifications. However, entering, operating, and exiting the elevator with an autonomous robot presents some challenges that must be addressed. This work analyzes the experimental results, and the detected problems during practical experimentation with an omnidirectional mobile robot while interacting with an elevator. Various solutions are proposed for the detected issues. The validation results show that the mobile robot evaluated can reliably and repeatably use the elevator.

articleTitle: Optimal Function Block Distribution for IEC 61499 Distributed Control Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The efficient distribution of function blocks across programmable logic controllers (PLCs) is critical to improving the performance of distributed automation systems. This paper presents a novel randomized greedy optimization algorithm to minimize communication latency and maximize resource utilization by optimizing the allocation of function blocks across multiple PLCs in compliance with the IEC 61499 standard. Simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach in achieving substantial performance improvements in distributed control applications. The results highlight the flexibility and scalability of the proposed optimization method, particularly in environments with varying PLC configurations.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Decentralized Variable Gain Robust Control Giving Consideration to Transient Behavior for Uncertain Large-Scale Serially Connected Systems via Piecewise Lyapunov Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this paper, a design method for decentralized robust controllers giving consideration to transient behavior for uncertain large-scale serially connected systems via piecewise Lyapunov functions (PLFs) is proposed. The proposed control law consists of a state feedback law and a compensation input with uniformly continuous functions. In our approach, chattering phenomenon in the control input is avoided by utilizing uniformly continuous functions. In this paper, we show that a sufficient condition for the existence of the proposed decentralized variable gain robust controller is reduced to linear matrix inequalities (LMIs).

articleTitle: An Adaptive Genetic Algorithm for Tension Control in Air-Jet Weaving Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In air-jet weaving, precise control of warp yarn tension is essential for maintaining both production quality and efficiency. Traditional control algorithms often exhibit low accuracy due to the time-varying characteristics of the warp-feeding system and the presence of external disturbances. To mitigate this limitation, a collaborative tension control model was developed by integrating the dynamics of the warp feed motor and yarn mechanics. A genetic algorithm was employed to optimize the three parameters of the PID controller, incorporating an adaptive crossover-mutation operator and simulated annealing to enhance the global search capabilities. Simulation and experimental results demonstrated that this method significantly improved tension stability and accuracy in comparison to conventional algorithms,

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence-Based User Interaction Module for Autonomous Mobile Service Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: With the evolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies, there is a growing demand for Intelligent Personal Assistants (IPAs) that allow fluid communication with humans. However, there are still several challenges to overcome, such as difficulty in understanding nuances in some contexts. Therefore, this study seeks to mitigate these gaps by presenting a modular and scalable architecture for integrating IPAs into autonomous service robots. The architecture allows communication between various robot systems and peripherals with AI mechanisms, including Large Language Model (LLM) and Natural Language Processing, which seek to improve the user experience. The proposed architecture was applied to developing a service robot designed to guide and interact with people in a university environment, incorporating the RASA framework with an LLM for natural language processing and response generation. The paper discusses the adopted technologies, the current state of development, the difficulties encountered, and the analysis of the first feedback from volunteers.

articleTitle: Prediction of Network Controllability Robustness Based on Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The controllability of complex networks has received extensive attention and in-depth research. The problem of controllability robustness is an important topic in the research on the controllability of networks. We propose a graph neural network model for network controllability robustness (NCR-GNN), which aims to predict the proportion of critical edges in networks, which is a key indicator for quantifying the controllability robustness of networks. The NCR-GNN model is a multi-layer graph neural network architecture that incorporates an average degree encoder. This encoder provides an initial feature embedding for the graph, utilizing both node degree and global degree information to efficiently capture the network's structural characteristics at both local and global levels. We incorporate aggregation methods derived from several well-established graph neural network (GNN) models, including the Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), Graph Attention Network (GAT), Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN), Chebyshev Network (ChebNet) and Topology Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network (TAG) into the NCR-GNN framework. Experimental results based on models and real networks show that the NCR-GNN model based on the ChebNet-aggregation method outperforms others in terms of training, validation, and test performance, demonstrating excellent generalization capabilities. This shows that the NCR-GNN model based on the ChebNet-aggregation method is suitable for the prediction task of network controllability robustness. Our NCR-GNN model provides an effective and adaptable framework to predict network controllability robustness, which has important potential applications in network science and engineering.

articleTitle: Energy-Saving Optimization of HVAC Cooling Source System Based on Predictive Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The operation of the cooling source system in the central heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system is associated with substantial energy consumption and carbon emissions. Therefore, it is of great significance to research energy-saving optimization of the cooling source system. The cooling source system comprises many devices, with complex coupling between subsystems. These characteristics make it challenging to formulate energy-saving optimization strategies, and the system faces challenges in maintaining consistent high-performance operation. To address these issues, this paper establishes models for the cooling source system and proposes an energy-saving optimization method based on predictive information fusion. The proposed method successfully reduces the energy consumption of the system. We validate the proposed method using actual field operation data, demonstrating its ability to ensure smooth system operation and effectively reduce energy consumption.

articleTitle: An Event-Trigger-Based Variable Gain Robust Formation Control for Multi-Agent Systems with Mismatched Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a design method for an event-trigger-based robust formation controller for multi-agent systems (MASs) with mismatched uncertainties. The multi-agent system under consideration has a leader-follower structure. The pro-posed control law consists of stabilizing state feedback inputs, state feedback inputs for consensus, and compensation inputs with adjustable parameters, and is designed by explicitly taking relative positions into account. In this paper, we show that sufficient conditions for the existence of the proposed robust formation control system are provided in terms of Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs).

articleTitle: Integration of Advanced Process Control into Modular Plants Using the Module Type Package
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Optimized and decentralized process control is crucial for energy systems incorporating renewable energy, as it enhances flexibility and reliability by dynamically managing variable energy inputs like solar and wind. This ensures optimal resource utilization and supports grid stability while minimizing environmental impact. However, the integration of external applications (e.g., for operational optimization) into existing process control systems for energy systems is cumbersome due to missing interfaces. This paper presents a novel approach to integrate Advanced Process Control applications into process control systems within modular production plants for energy systems using the Module Type Package standard. The proposed integration framework facilitates system integration and enhances scalability, particularly in complex and dynamic industrial environments. The framework reduces manual configuration efforts and improves the operational efficiency of modular plants by enabling standardized and reliable communication between Advanced Process Control systems and process control systems. The proposed framework is validated through a case study on modular electrolysis plants, demonstrating its effectiveness in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Support Vector Machine-Based False Data Injection Attacks Detection in Interconnected DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The integration of multiple DC microgrids offers a robust solution for modern energy needs, especially with the high penetration of intermittent renewable sources. However, the reliance on extensive communication networks for coordinating Multiple interlinking converters (MICs) in these microgrids introduces vulnerabilities, particularly to False Data Injection Attacks (FDIAs), which can compromise system stability and security. This paper presents an AI-based anomaly detection strategy utilizing Support Vector Machines (SVM) at the primary control level to detect FDIAs in clustered DC microgrids. The proposed SVM model, trained offline with a comprehensive dataset of operational and attack scenarios, effectively delineates boundaries between normal and attack-induced conditions, enabling real-time detection in the online phase. Upon identifying an FDIA, the system decouples the primary control and transitions to a localized power balancing control, effectively preserving microgrid stability. Extensive simulations validate the efficacy of the proposed approach, demonstrating its ability to sustain stable microgrid operation under various FDIA scenarios, including time-varying and unbounded attacks.

articleTitle: A Transformer-Based Deep Learning Framework for Early Classification and Operator Decision Support
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: An industrial alarm flood indicates a critical issue within a process that requires prompt and effective action. However, responding effectively in such situations can be difficult, particularly when alarm rates are high and contextual insights are lacking. Thus, a deep learning framework is introduced in this paper to provide decision support to industrial operators during an alarm flood. The proposed framework is mainly implemented in the following steps: 1) A textual vectorization method is proposed to transform alarms into numerical representations suitable for deep learning applications; 2) Clusters of similar historical sequences are identified based on the modified Frobenius distance; and 3) A transformer-based model is employed to early classify ongoing alarm floods and provide decision support to industrial operators. The effectiveness of this approach is validated using real industrial data from an oil refinery.

articleTitle: Distributed Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Task Scheduling in Multi-Robot Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: With the increasing task scale and dynamic complexity of multi-robot systems in automated production lines, we design a dynamic distributed task scheduling framework to accelerate the convergence of the combinatorial optimization model, which is suitable for time-varying multi-task and multi-robot scenarios. By integrating an empirical learning model and a teammate collaboration model, a distributed deep reinforcement learning algorithm is formulated with a limited number of workstations. Each workstation is designed as an independent agent, interacting with the environment to learn the current allocation state of robots. Then, a Q-learning network is trained to extract high-dimensional features from the state and optimize the task scheduling policy. Besides, a greedy strategy is incorporated with the Q-learning network to favor actions that show an increasing trend in Q-values, which enables the algorithm to prioritize higher-priority tasks when facing resource limitations. Simulations with three different workload intensities demonstrate that our algorithm achieves a respective enhancement in overall performance of 3.50%, 8.16%, and 3.86% compared with the foundational deep reinforcement learning models.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Target Tracking of Unmanned Surface Vessels With Input Saturation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In this article, we develop a finite-time target tracking scheme for unmanned surface vessels (USVs) facing external disturbances and input saturation. The target's dynamics are unknown, with only line-of-sight range and angle measurements available. First, we design a kinematic control law using finite-time extended state observers (ESOs) to estimate the uncertain target's dynamics. Then, we design a dynamics control law based on a finite-time adaptive sliding mode disturbance observer to estimate the unknown external disturbances affecting the follower. Additionally, we design auxiliary systems using fractional power to address actuator constraints and achieve finite-time convergence. Simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed bounded controller in tracking a moving target.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Prediction of GAT201-Regulated Gene Expression in Cryptococcus Neoformans Using Minimal Motifs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Cryptococcal meningitis, caused by Cryptococcus neoformans, leads to around 200,000 deaths annually. GAT201 regulates growth and defence mechanisms in C. neoformans. However, not all genes are highly impacted by GAT201. Identifying highly-impacted genes and predicting their gene expression levels are two typical research challenges. In this paper, to address these challenges, we first develop an integrated statistic approach (i.e., negative binomial regression, the Wilcoxon test, and DESeq2) and outlier correlation method to identify highly-impacted genes. Second, an efficient gene identification model using logistic regression was built, which can identify unseen highly-impacted genes utilising a minimal number of motifs. Besides, gene expression prediction models consisting of negative binomial regression and principal component regression methods were developed to predict genes' expression levels separately. Experiments implemented on a benchmark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, improve our understanding of the regulatory role of GAT201, and provide new possibilities for the treatment of diseases associated with Cryptococcus neoformans.

articleTitle: Chiller Fault Diagnosis Method with Limited Data Based on Graph Interpolation Enhanced Graph Attention Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The fault diagnosis of chillers holds significant importance in minimizing operational costs and energy consumption. However, due to the scarcity of labeled samples, many intelligent fault diagnosis methods fail to achieve optimal performance. To address this problem, a graph attention network fault diagnosis method based on graph interpolation enhancement is proposed. In the proposed method, the sliding window segmentation is applied to limited data initially, and then the sensors are utilized as nodes and the corresponding data as node features to construct a fully connected graph, followed by the use of graph interpolation method for data enhancement. Subsequently, the correlation between node features is leveraged to obtain a sparse graph. Next, the processed graph samples are input into a two-layer graph attention network for message passing and aggregation. Afterward, the node feature representations are aggregated into the whole graph representation through concatenation and readout operations for graph classification. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been validated on the authoritative dataset ASHRAE RP1043. The experimental results demonstrate this method has superior diagnostic performance compared to traditional approaches.

articleTitle: Real-Time Fault Diagnosis: A Transformer-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Fault diagnosis in process control and monitoring is crucial for ensuring safety and maintaining operational efficiency. Faults represent deviations from the normal trajectory of the system, indicating potential issues that require timely intervention. However, current fault diagnosis methods often encounter delays or low accuracy with many hyper parameters to tune, limiting their applicability and generalizability in real-world industrial settings, particularly in high-frequency data environments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an online fault diagnosis strategy based on a modified transformer architecture, which is specifically tailored for time-series classification. By considering fault diagnosis as a classification problem, the proposed model provides real-time fault diagnosis in a highly parallelizable manner without introducing any systematic delays, which is crucial for maintaining seamless operation. This approach also mitigates real-world challenges such as missing data, asynchronous data flow, and delays. Leveraging deep-learning techniques, the proposed approach harnesses the in-herent parallelizability of attention-based models to enable rapid fault diagnosis without compromising accuracy. Furthermore, to increase the classification accuracy, a two-step training procedure is employed. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, it is compared with other well-established fault diagnosis methods using the extended Tennessee Eastman Process Dataset. This research highlights the power of deep learning in enhancing fault diagnosis capabilities, paving the way for safer and more efficient industrial operations.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of a Multi-Degree-of-Freedom Energy Harvester for Mechanical Vibrations Based on Coupled Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This work describes a model for multi-degrees-of-freedom energy harvesters for ambient mechanical vibrations, based on coupled resonators that form a networked structure. The governing equations of motions for the model are derived, and stochastic calculus along with numerical simulations are used for their analysis. A power balance equation obeying a fluctuation-dissipation theorem is given. At steady state, the power injected in the harvester by random vibrations is partially dissipated by internal friction, and partially transferred to an electrical load. It is also shown that all these quantities can be calculated by solving a Lyapunov matrix equation. An algorithm based on the steepest ascent method is used to optimize the harvester. Because an analytic formula for the harvested power is not available, the derivatives for the gradient estimation are calculated numerically. The algorithm converges fast, and is very efficient, giving a significant advantage in optimization problems where a large parameter space must be explored. Finally, it is shown that the networked structure harvests significantly more power with respect to a single-degree-of-freedom system.

articleTitle: From Raw Data to Monotonic and Trendable Features Reflecting Degradation Trends in Turbofan Engines
