publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The performance of prognostic models relies heavily on the form and trend of the extracted features. However, the raw data collected from physical systems are inherently noisy, large in volume, and exhibit significant variability, which makes them unsuitable for direct use in prognostics. These characteristics poorly reflect the degradation behavior of physical systems and contribute to the uncertainty of prognostic outcome. Hence, transforming this data into relevant features and carefully selecting them is crucial for meeting the specific needs of prognostic models. This paper aims to address data processing challenges by focusing on extraction and selection of high-quality monotonic features which clearly reflect the degradation and can reduce prognostics uncertainty. The proposed framework comprises three main stages: Data pre-processing, feature extraction, and feature selection. It includes a fitness analysis to evaluate the monotonicity and trendability of features supplemented by visual inspections to identify relevant features. Applied to the Commercial Modular Aero-Propulsion System Simulation (CMAPSS) dataset from the NASA Ames Prognostics Data Repository, the framework reduces noise, improves feature monotonicity and trendability, and facilitates the selection of useful features - essential aspects for effective prognostic methods.

articleTitle: Advances in the Smart Data Analytics Framework: Integrating Data Extraction and Automated Reporting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The efficient fusion of information from different data silos in a process plant is essential for a smart data analytics platform. Researchers have developed a GUI-based framework, namely, AMtool, to integrate alarm data and sensor (process) data complemented with process connectivity information. This state-of-the-art smart data analytics framework integrates advanced techniques for data analysis and visualization, performance evaluation, and alarm configuration. This framework also supports alarm flood analysis along with documentation to aid alarm rationalization, enabling industrial processes to become compliant with industry standards. However, an earlier version of the AMtool faced limitations in meeting the automation and real-time data exchange requirements emphasized by the Industry 4.0 paradigm. In this paper, we discuss the recent advances and improvements to make the tool compliant with Industry 4.0 standards, namely, the data extraction interface and automated reporting feature. The data extraction interface facilitates secure and efficient data collection via SQL databases and OPC UA platforms. Additionally, the report generation is more automated for an efficient and more user-friendly option for the regular generation of alarm analysis reports.

articleTitle: Optimal Redundant Transmission-Based Defense Against Reverse Attacks with a Game Theory Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper studies a redundant transmission-based defense strategy against reverse attacks on remote state estimation. Firstly, a game-theoretic framework is developed, allowing both the adversary and defender to select multiple channels for attacking and transmitting data. Secondly, within the proposed framework, a zero-sum game, a general-sum game, and a Bayesian game are formulated depending on the defender's knowledge of the attacker's cost. Finally, the Nash and Bayesian Nash equilibria of the three games are analyzed and computed to identify the optimal strategies for both the attacker and defender. Numerical simulations are conducted to demonstrate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Traffic Classification in Software-Defined Networking (SDN): Application of Machine Learning Models for Flooding DDoS Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Among the advantages offered by the SDN paradigm over traditional networks is the centralized implementation of comprehensive security policies. From this perspective, this study develops, trains, and tests several machine learning algorithms for traffic classification, distinguishing between legitimate traffic and three types of DDoS flooding attacks (HTTP, UDP, and TCP). The dataset used for training was employed both in its raw and preprocessed forms, and was generated in a reference study. The Random Forest and Gradient Boosting algorithms achieved the highest results in terms of accuracy and F1-score. Additionally, a comparison of the results of the studies is conducted.

articleTitle: The Impact of Capacity Adequacy Constraints in Planning Models for Different RES Penetration Levels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper investigates the evolving impact of resource adequacy constraints in capacity expansion planning (CEP) models, as renewable energy sources (RES) penetration targets increase. To do so, a CEP model is developed and implemented for various scenarios of RES penetration levels both with and without incorporating adequacy-oriented constraints. The resulting outcomes are then compared to highlight the variations in the optimal generation mix between scenarios, demonstrating how the inclusion or exclusion of adequacy constraints affects the generation mix across different RES penetrations. The analysis reveals that, at RES penetration levels below 75%, thermal units play a critical role in maintaining system adequacy. However, beyond 75% penetration, storage technologies, such as batteries and pumped hydro storage, take over to ensure adequacy. Additionally, a sensitivity analysis is conducted under the assumption that RES do not contribute to system adequacy, representing a conservative scenario for system reliability. In this case, thermal units remain in the generation mix, even at 100% RES penetration, solely to meet adequacy requirements without contributing to energy generation.

articleTitle: Multi-Dimensional Layers Framework for Classifying Waste in Industrial Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The transition from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0 introduces new challenges in waste management, particularly digital, energy and human waste. However its not clear how to classify and categorize without creating new dilemmas in the 8 traditional established wastes from Lean theory. To solve this problem, this paper aims to develop a multi-dimensional layers framework to classify waste by making a interpretation of the traditional lean principles into a digital and sustainable layer perspective. The methodology involves projecting the 8 lean wastes onto physical, digital, and sustainable layers, allowing for a comprehensive waste characterization. With this, its presented a framework that identifies various types of digital waste, such as defective data and excessive non-value-adding data, and highlights the energy inefficiencies and human factors associated with digital transformation. The results shows the framework's ability to provide a n organized approach to attempt to classification new wastes typologies without creating new wastes and keeping the Lean theory at its original state. As such, this study contributes to the literature by expanding the concept of digital waste and integrating sustainability into waste typology and providing the implications of the layer expansion for future research.

articleTitle: A Cost-Effective Solution for Predictive Maintenance in Industrial Pumping Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper presents a cost-effective, Internet of Things (IoT)-based solution for predictive maintenance (PdM) in industrial pumping systems. The proposed system integrates custom-built hardware with machine learning (ML) algorithms to monitor and detect anomalies in real-time. The innovation of the system lies in its non-intrusive design, ease of installation, and adaptability to a variety of industrial environments, providing a practical, low-cost alternative to traditional PdM solutions. Detailed discussion is provided on the hardware component selection, which prioritizes affordability without sacrificing performance, as well as the machine learning strategies used for anomaly detection. Preliminary results from laboratory and field testing demonstrate the system's potential for reducing downtime and maintenance costs, with a focus on extending the application to broader industrial contexts.

articleTitle: Enhancing Traffic Signal State Retrieval Reliability in Autonomous Buses Using a Dual-Camera System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In the context of urban intelligent transportation systems (ITS), ensuring that autonomous buses can follow traffic flow to safeguard passenger safety is fundamental. To achieve this, these buses must accurately obtain the current status of traffic control systems, such as traffic signals. The advanced methods of traffic signal recognition typically rely on computer vision and pattern recognition algorithms, which allow the autonomous vehicle to gather information similarly to a human driver without requiring modifications to existing infrastructure. However, these algorithms face challenges like high computational demands, failure to recognize objects outside the camera's field of view, glare, low light, noise, or poor image quality. This study aims to explore methods for improving traffic signal information retrieval by enhancing existing computer vision-based recognition or through the integration of radio-based data acquisition. A proposed solution combines dual-camera systems with radio-based data collection, offering a more reliable and efficient traffic signal recognition system. This approach effectively enhances the safety of urban ITSs by leveraging a fusion of computer vision and radio technology.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Path Following of AUVs: A Multiobjective Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper addresses the path following problem of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) under input and state constraints, propose a novel multiobjective model predictive optimization control scheme. First, by treating path parameters as decision variables, it introduces an innovative real-time optimization of reference states, ensuring both accuracy and efficiency in path tracking. Second, to address varying task priorities, a constraint weighted sum (CWS) method is developed. This approach effectively resolves priority conflicts within the multiobjective model predictive control (MOMPC) framework, significantly improving control performance and flexibility for AUVs in complex environments. These advancements offer new technical support for both theoretical research and practical applications in AUVs path tracking. Then, through rigorous theoretical analysis, the feasibility and stability of the MOMPC path following control algorithm are demonstrated. Finally, simulation studies on the AUVs validate the effectiveness of the proposed MOMPC path following control method.

articleTitle: High-Probability Feedback Controllers from Data with Stochastic Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: A central challenge in data-driven control is effectively leveraging different types of data. This work addresses the design of state feedback controllers for unknown systems using data corrupted by stochastic disturbances. First, we link the distribution of system parameters consistent with noisy data to the stochastic disturbances by reconstructing the data. Based on the distribution of the disturbances, we develop a data-driven formulation that characterizes admissible systems under probability constraints. Then, with this probabilistic description of the underlying system dynamics, a tractable problem in the form of linear matrix inequalities is formulated to evaluate the likelihood that a given feedback gain stabilizes the unknown system. Additionally, a data-driven optimization problem is proposed to co-design the stabilizing probability and feedback gain. This approach facilitates the design of a reliable state feedback controller with a high probability of stabilization. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the proposed co-design method guarantees an increase in the stabilizing probability with the collection of new data. Finally, numerical examples are presented to illustrate the advantages of the proposed controller design approach.

articleTitle: Second-Order Sliding Mode Trajectory Tracking Control of Autonomous Surface Vehicles Under Influence of Unknown Ocean Currents
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This article explores the trajectory tracking control challenge faced by autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs), which are affected by unknown ocean currents. To counterbalance the impacts of mismatched perturbations, hybrid second-order sliding mode (SOSM) controller according to switching strategy is developed which switches from prescribed time second-order sliding mode controller to conventional finite time second-order sliding mode controller. The former ensures that the sliding variables converge to closed tight set at the zero in prescribed time and the convergence time does not depend on the initial states of the system, while the latter facilitates the convergence of the sliding variables to zero in finite time. Finally, the analysis of closed-loop system stability is conducted and the theoretical results are validated through numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Discrete Controller Design in Grid Following Converters for Guaranteed Performance and Robustness Against Weak Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This work introduces a direct discrete-time multi-variable control strategy for grid-connected power converters using LCL filters in grid-following mode, specifically designed to manage inherent delays and prevent hidden oscillations in discrete implementation. It addresses the challenges of managing converter output current while considering grid variations and uncertainties introduced by other elements such as the Phase-Locked Loop (PLL), as well as the inherent delay in computation and Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) signal generation. The controller is defined as an structures state feedback control without the need of an observer, and it is designed to address the compromise between robustness (by minimizing the H-infinity norm of the sensitivity function), speed response (by guaranteeing a given decay rate), and noise amplification (by limiting the range of gain values). The gain computation is carried out by iteratively solving a set of Linear Matrix Inequalities problems through a Cone Complementarity Linearization. The proposed strategy is compared to traditional Proportional-Integral (PI) plus decouplers and feedforward temrs structures through comprehensive simulations, demonstrating its improved ability to handle weak grid scenarios.

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation of High-Fidelity Models of IPMSM Drive Systems in Offline and Real-Time Simulators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) are widely used in industrial applications, electric propulsion and precision applications. Accurate and efficient simulations of IPMSM drives are essential for the design and tuning of such systems. Field-oriented control (FOC) is commonly used to achieve precise control by decoupling the stator currents into flux- and torque-controlling components. The FOC-based controllers, however, require addressing the nonlinear flux-current relationships in IPMSMs caused by saliency, magnetic saturation, and cross-coupling effects. Different methods, such as parameter estimation and look-up tables (LUTs) techniques, are used to model these nonlinearities, with LUTs offering accuracy but demanding substantial memory allocation. Alternatively, memory-compact models such as polynomial-based models are used when systems impose constraints on memory allocation. This paper presents the efficient implementation of both the LUT-based and polynomial-based IPMSM drive system models for offline and real-time simulators. The accuracy of the models is verified through offline studies performed in MATLAB/Simulink and OPAL-RT's OP5700 real-time simulator. The obtained results demonstrate the difference in system resource utilization, such as memory requirement and computational efficiency, when using LUT-based and polynomial-based IPMSM models.

articleTitle: A Multi-Channel Adaptive Cancellation Algorithm for Active Suppression of Motion-Induced Noise in Magnetic Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: During super low frequency (SLF) magnetic induction communication, the sensitive antenna carried by autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) is highly susceptible to vibration, resulting in a large amount of noise in communication signals, which seriously affects communication performance. The type of motion-induced noise typically exhibits randomness and nonlinearity. Based on the strong correlation between the motion-induced noise and the antenna's vibration signal, we propose a multi-channel normalized least mean square (MCNLMS) algorithm. The algorithm utilizes the six degrees of freedom vibration acceleration information from both ends of the magnetic antenna as the reference signal input for the canceller, providing more comprehensive information related to motion-induced noise than the single-channel adaptive noise cancellation algorithm. Experimental results indicate that the MCNLMS algorithm demonstrates effective suppression of the motion-induced noise, achieving an average reduction of approximately 7 dB within the 160–170 Hz communication band. Additionally, it exhibits improved stability and faster convergence.

Author Keywords: multi-channel normalized least mean squares algorithm

articleTitle: A Cooling Load Interval Prediction Method Based on the FCM-QRLSTM Hybrid Model for Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Accurate cooling load prediction is fundamental to optimizing energy utilization, in the context of rapid development towards ecological civilization, enhancing the accuracy of cooling load prediction technologies for building air conditioning systems and optimizing their practical applications is particularly important. This study proposes a cooling load interval prediction method based on fuzzy c-means (FCM) and quantile regression long short-term memory (QRLSTM) hybrid model for buildings to address issues such as data missing or inaccurate schedules that lead to uneven load distribution, and to accurately quantify the fluctuations in building air conditioning cooling loads. First, Pearson correlation analysis is employed to select relevant input features. In addition, the FCM clustering algorithm is utilized to preprocess historical cooling load data in the training set, alleviating the imbalance in load distribution. Finally, the QRLSTM interval prediction method is applied to predict cooling loads, revealing their inherent volatility and uncertainty. The results demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits significant advantages in both the accuracy of point predictions and the performance of interval predictions.

articleTitle: Stability Study of the Three-Phase Implementation of the Unicon Control in the Stationary Reference Frame for Grid Forming Inverters in Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Electronic converters connected to a microgrid must contribute to its stability while sharing the load proportionally of their nominal power. This contribution presents the Universal Control technique in a Stationary Reference Frame (UCStRf). The UCStRf is a control technique that implements the power-to-frequency droop law for inverters connected to a microgrid while implementing an output virtual impedance loop to ensure the stability of the converter in spite of variations of the microgrid parameters. Section II presents the UCStRf control technique; section III details the virtual output impedance design criteria; section IV develops the small-signal model of the Active Power Loop (APL); section V details the design of the control loops to ensure the stability criteria; and section VI validates the proposed control scheme by means of simulations.

articleTitle: Alarm Root-Cause Analysis Using an Alarm Logic Directed Graph Extracted From Control Software
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The growing complexity of modern automated production systems demands solutions for managing alarm floods potentially stemming from multi-root causes, while improving situational awareness of operators to ensure timely fault responses and minimize downtime. For this purpose, knowledge-driven approaches that utilize domain specific knowledge for alarm handling have shown promising results. However, knowledge extraction is expensive, leaving data-driven approaches as an alternative, which in turn requires large amounts of data. To profit from both approaches and alleviate their weaknesses, hybrid approaches have been a focus of recent development. Therefore, this work proposes the Alarm-Logic-Directed-Graph for a novel hybrid approach. This graph models the alarm logic inherent in the control code, enabling knowledge-based clustering and sorting of the alarm log, which then serves as input data for a subsequent Bayesian network learning. Moreover, with the integration of physical and heuristic knowledge, the root causes can be further refined to alarm-related component status variables. The evaluation of this work is conducted on the Tennessee-Eastman Process, a well-known continuous process simulation. The results show that the proposed approach remains robust to multi-root cause identification even in the absence of historical alarm log data or process knowledge besides programmable logic controller code.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Event-Triggered Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: In recent decades, with the rapid development of machine learning, more and more research fields have combined machine learning to seek mathematical tools that are more suitable for application. Among them, reinforcement learning which is in the field of machine learning shows significant advantages in complex environment decision making. However, as the environment becomes more complicated, reinforcement learning also faces the problem of slow convergence. The event-triggered theory has become a new field in control science in the last ten years, which aims to reduce the high energy consumption and large computation of traditional periodic control methods. The two theories complement each other to some extent. Then, we show the principle and innovation of combining the event-triggered theory with the actor-critic, also give the mathematical representation of the event-triggered mechanism and the convergence proof of the event-triggered actor-critic, as well as the flow of the event-triggered actor-critic algorithm. Finally, the correctness of the theory is further verified through data-based simulation on the Garnet environment. We also discuss the direction of the improvement of the theory and future work.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach to Payload Heave Motion Prediction Under Irregular Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Effective handling of the payload with an offshore crane is critical for ensuring safety and efficiency in the offshore operation. Accurate modelling of payload heave motion is essential for safeguarding transportation and improving feedback control for active heave compensation. Traditional kinematic modelling fails to account for the nonlinear dynamics of waveinduced motion. This paper proposes a data-driven method, leveraging real motion data from the Norwegian Motion Lab, to predict payload heave positions based on ship heave positions. Extensive experiments are carried out using a diverse dataset under various sea states, and the proposed method is evaluated against three methods from different disciplines. The results demonstrate that the data-driven approach outperforms the compared methods, showing a better overall performance across multiple wave scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhancing Steganography Image Quality with Six-Bit LSB and Operator Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The rapid advancement of electronic technology has driven the digitization of various data forms, creating a greater need for secure data management to protect privacy and prevent unauthorized reproduction. Cryptography and steganography are commonly employed to meet these needs: cryptography encrypts data, while steganography conceals information within cover files, such as images, to enable secure communication. This study builds on existing image steganography solutions by improving the quality of stego images using the Least Significant Bit (LSB) approach, known for its simplicity and high data capacity. The proposed method embeds secret data into cover images and includes an optimized extraction process to enhance the visual quality of the stego image. Experimental results show a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of up to 66.680 dB and an average improvement of 17.64%, outperforming existing methods with comparable payload capacities.

articleTitle: Real-Time Automated Logging of Manual Interventions in Autonomous Buses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Automated intervention logging plays a crucial role in enhancing the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems. This paper presents a novel automated system for recording driver interventions during the operation of autonomous buses. The system integrates real-time sensor data, including steering, braking, and Global Positioning System (GPS) coordinates, to automatically log and analyze manual interventions. The proposed method was validated during an autonomous bus pilot in Fukaya City, Saitama Prefecture, Japan, where manual human interventions were necessary to avoid obstacles and adapt to changing environmental conditions. By automating the intervention recording process, the system reduces the labor-intensive manual logging traditionally required in autonomous driving trials, thus improving data accuracy and operational efficiency. The results demonstrate that the system enhances the ability to monitor and analyze critical intervention points, particularly in complex urban traffic environments, making it a valuable tool for advancing the integrity of autonomous bus technologies.

articleTitle: Extended and Unscented Kalman Filter Based Estimation of State-of-Charge of Li-Ion Batteries Using 3-RC Equivalent Circuit Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The growing presence of electric vehicles (EVs) in the market has spurred investigations into various algorithms for estimating the state-of-charge (SoC) of the battery. Accurately estimating the SoC is of paramount importance for the battery management systems. This paper conducts an exhaustive literature review on diverse methods for SoC estimation, recognizing the critical importance of an accurate battery model in enhancing prediction efficiency. The study introduces and evaluates three methods, a) Coulomb Counting, b) Extended Kalman Filter and c) Unscented Kalman Filter for SoC estimation. Through simulation, the paper presents and analyzes the results derived from these methods. To simulate a Li-ion battery model, a 3-RC battery model was developed utilizing the Equivalent Circuit Model method. SoC estimation is conducted on a Li-ion battery with a capacity of 31A and voltage of 10.8V. In the simulations, a constant current charging method at 1C rate was employed for charging, while discharging was executed at various rates depending on the SoC of the battery, utilizing a random pulse generator and noise to replicate real-world scenarios. The UKF outperforms the EKF due to its ability to effectively handle highly nonlinear battery dynamics, thus yielding more accurate SoC estimations over time.

articleTitle: Critical Comparison of Solid and Flexible Press-Fit Zones Based on Mechanical Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The pursuit of electrification in recent years has accelerated trends like miniaturization and connectivity. This has prompted the electrical connector industry to adopt press-fit zones more extensively in the race for electrification. The utilization of press-fit zones offers several advantages, including simpler assembly, re-usability, and enhanced reliability. In the automotive industry, press-fit zones are widely used in various applications, extending beyond the electrified powertrain and encompassing everyday components such as steering wheels, airbags, and ABS systems. Although hybrid electric vehicles frequently utilize press-fit zones, their usage is not limited to the mundane domains. Among the various press-fit shapes, the most prevalent ones are the solid press-fit zones with a square cross-section and the flexible press-fit zones resembling an eye of a needle (EON). The focus in literature has traditionally been on comparing the electrical aspects of solid and EON zones. However, it is essential to acknowledge that mechanical parameters, such as geometry, material, and manufacturing techniques, play a significant role in influencing the final electrical performance of these press fit zones. These mechanical factors can have a substantial impact on the overall functionality and reliability of the connectors, and therefore should not be overlooked when considering their performance and compatibility for specific applications. After a thorough evaluation, press-fit zones were carefully selected and analyzed based on a range of mechanical parameters. The results obtained from this analysis serve as a fundamental reference for choosing the appropriate zones for specific applications. By considering these mechanical factors, engineers and designers can make informed decisions, ensuring that the selected press-fit zones align perfectly with the requirements and demands of each particular use case. This approach enhances the overall performance, reliability, and efficiency of the connectors in their intended applications.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Cost-Efficient Power Control in Multi-Cell Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Energy consumption is a critical concern in multi-cell networks. To reduce the energy cost, renewable energy has been accommodated to offer cellular networks with auxiliary energy supply. Most existing studies of cellular networks powered by hybrid energy sources are based on ideal battery models. However, the energy storage efficiency of batteries in reality is influenced by environmental factors and the natural degradation of batteries over time. In this paper, we investigate the cost-efficient transmit power control in multi-cell networks with hybrid energy sources and time-varying energy storage efficiency. Considering such dynamic networks characterized by the stochastic property of energy harvesting, channel conditions, and time-varying energy storage efficiency, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is adopted to learn the optimal power control strategy without requiring prior knowledge of the environment. To enhance the robustness and accommodate varying levels of exploration and exploitation during different training phases of DRL, an enhanced proximal policy optimization algorithm is proposed. Specifically, a dynamic clipping threshold is designed based on an adaptive adjustment mechanism, which allows modifying the clipping threshold in accordance with the agent's performance. Simulation results show that our proposed DRL algorithm can significantly improve the cost efficiency of the multi-cell network compared with other DRL algorithms.

articleTitle: A Decoupled Complementary Design Framework for Robust Tracking Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Robust tracking control for unstable or non-minimum phase systems with unknown disturbance and/or modeling uncertainty is well-known to be challenging. In this paper, a new complementary design framework is proposed to achieve robust tracking control. The proposed controller consists of two parts: an inner loop control which stabilizes the plant while also conducting compensation of disturbance/uncertainty at the same time, and an outer loop nominal tracking control which can be designed with the existing methods based on the stabilized plant model without disturbance/uncertainty. The purpose of the inner loop compensation is, hence, to suppress the impacts of disturbance/uncertainty on the plant so that the nominal tracking performance could be recovered in an environment with unknown disturbance/uncertainty. Since the design of outer loop tracking control is conducted on the compensated plant model, the challenge is eliminated effectively for the robust tracking control of unstable or non-minimum phase plants. Simulations are presented to show the superior tracking performance with much improved robustness.

articleTitle: Resilient and Robust Model Predictive Tracking Control for ASVs under Asynchronous DoS Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative resilient model predictive control (MPC) approach for trajectory tracking control problem of autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) under continuous dual channels denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. These attacks which could adversely affect the tracking performance of ASVs disrupt both the communications from the controller to the actuator (C-A) and from the sensor to the controller (S-C). In order to solve the above problem, an extended sequential transmission strategy is designed to counteract the loss of communication due to DoS attacks in the C-A channel, ensuring the stability of the system, and we develop an estimator to estimate state to solve the problem of state information loss under S-C channel DoS attacks. Additionally, to cope with external disturbances, an optimization problem with tightened constraint is designed. Theoretical analysis confirms feasibility and the closed-loop stability for ASVs. Through simulations and comparisons, we demonstrate that our strategy sustains system stability and robustness against complex cyber threats.

articleTitle: Logarithmic Sliding-Mode Observer and Controller for Position Sensorless PMSM Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Accurate acquisition of rotor position information is vital for sensorless field-oriented control (FOC) of the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). The sliding-mode observer (SMO) method is widely used in medium- and high-speed motor operations due to its straightforward implementation and robustness. However, the discontinuous control law leads to chattering phenomenon which reduces the accuracy of position estimation. In this paper, the logarithmic sliding-mode (LnSM) observer is proposed for estimating rotor position and the super-twisting algorithm (STA)-based LnSM (STA-LnSM) controller is designed to achieve fast and high-precision tracking of motor speed. Compared with the traditional SMO and PI controller, the proposed strategy significantly eliminates the effect of chattering phenomenon on the accuracy of rotor position estimation and improves the dynamic performance of the system. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: A Noise Label Correction Architecture for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The efficacy of deep learning in medical image segmentation is heavily reliant on large datasets with precise annotations. Yet, acquiring such data is costly and labor-intensive, and the annotations are often plagued by errors, particularly for subtle lesions. These inaccuracies can lead to artificial intelligence (AI) misdiagnoses in early-stage liver cancer. However, discarding noisy data will not only decrease the amount of data, but also degrade the performance of learning model. The available label correction methods may have label correction errors in the process of correcting noisy labels. To combat the limitations of noisy data and flawed label correction methods, we present the Confident Teacher Correction Network (CTCNet). CTCNet replaces unreliable labels with ‘soft’ labels that are refined during training to minimize noise. Our novel loss function mitigates the impact of high-variance predictions, reducing the uncertainty of predictions. CTCNet consists of two steps: (1) using the proposed shallow denoising subtraction network to remove background noise and learning high frequency information of small focus areas and (2) correcting the learning of noisy labels using a new loss function. We evaluated CTCNet on two public datasets of noise labels with different erasure rates. The results of the experiments showed that CTCNet had demonstrated superior performance over existing state-of-the-art methods. In particular, CTCNet does not require prior knowledge of noise characteristics, making it a robust and versatile solution. We can use CTCNet to assist the correction of the doctor's annotation, which can provide physicians and researchers with more reliable image annotation.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Button-Based Action Recognition Method Based on Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel keystroke action recognition method leveraging Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). Button-based action identification plays a critical role in various fields, including secure authentication, human-computer interaction, and device control, where accurate and efficient recognition of user input is essential. The proposed approach involves capturing data on triaxial acceleration, angular velocity, and quaternions during the 1.5 seconds following each keystroke, using an STM32 microcontroller and MPU6050 sensor. Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is applied to extract frequency-domain features, which are combined with time-domain information to provide a comprehensive feature set. By integrating temporal and spatial data, the model achieves high recognition efficiency. The architecture, which combines Bidirectional LSTM and 1D CNN layers, performs classification via a Softmax layer. Experimental results demonstrate over 99% accuracy in digit recognition, underscoring the model's robust capabilities and potential for broad application in scenarios requiring reliable button-based action identification.

articleTitle: Assessment of Current and Voltage Signature Analysis for the Diagnosis of Open-Switch Faults in Asymmetrical Six-Phase AC PMSM Drives for Electric Vehicles Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Multiphase traction inverters are receiving more and more interest in electrical powertrain applications where reliability and safety are key items. However, with the requirement of more switches, multiphase inverters are more exposed to different potential anomalies and more specifically open-switch faults. In this context, detecting inverter faults is necessary to guarantee the required efficiency. This paper deals with two approaches suitable for detecting open-switch faults in closed-loop controlled six-phase ac permanent magnet synchronous motor. Specifically, the paper is aimed to assess current and voltage signature analysis, evaluated in the αβ planes, for detecting and localizing inverter open-switch faults. It is shown that the presence of specific harmonics can affect significantly the diagnosis process. Here, a diagnostic space vector, elaborated in the fifth αβ plane is proposed to cope with this limitation. The established assessment has been analyzed by numerical simulations and experimentally validated.

articleTitle: TETR: Traversability Evaluation with Transformers for Autonomous Navigation in 3D Terrain Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Autonomous navigation of unmanned ground vehicles(UGVs) in complex three-dimensional terrains necessitates precise evaluation of road traversability, a challenge that remains unresolved due to the difficulty in quantifying passable regions. Existing methodologies often fall short in effectively evaluating traversability in complex environments. In this paper, we present a novel approach for evaluating terrain traversability by enabling the model to implicitly learn principle-based knowledge. The approach utilizes elevation maps obtained from equiped sensors of UGVs, capturing detailed terrain information through a novel transformer-based model, enabling accurate and efficient traversability assessments. We evaluated our method using a comprehensive simulation dataset, which achieves an accuracy of 93.1%, representing a 5.2% improvement over existing baseline method. Furthermore, our approach demonstrated a 16.9% reduction in computational overhead, facilitating real-time implementation.

articleTitle: Variable-Gain Extended State Observer-Based Data-Driven Trajectory Tracking Control of Unmanned Marine Vehicles Under Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: The traditional linear extended state observer (ESO) often suffers from the peaking phenomenon, which affects its observation accuracy and practicality. This paper proposes an improved variable-gain ESO (VGESO) to address disturbances estimation problem in trajectory tracking control for unmanned marine vehicles (UMVs), aiming to mitigate the trade-off between steady-state error and peaking phenomenon. Firstly, an equivalent data-driven model of UMVs subject to ocean disturbances is created using compact form dynamic linearization technique. Furthermore, a forgetting factor is introduced to enable the controller to respond more rapidly to the most recent input/output data while diminishing the influence of older, less significant information. What's more, the theory proves the stability of the tracking error system. Finally, simulation studies are presented to validate the main results.
